Its header comment highlights an important point: each character is drawn using lines ([<path>] elements), and never written as text (a [<text>] element); otherwise, a bot would simply have to read the image’s source code.

docs.title: 11.13.6. auth/captcha.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# auth/captcha.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A CAPTCHA ("test to distinguish a human from a robot") generated by the
# server itself, without an external service: a few distorted characters,
# obscured by lines, in an image SVG (see dessin_captcha.py). A
# A human can read them easily; a bot that simply sends
# forms over and over again cannot do so.
#
# How it works:
#    1. generer() generates a random text, turns it into an image, and stores the
#       correct answer EN MÉMOIRE DU SERVEUR, under a random ID;
#    2. The page displays the image and places the identifier in a hidden field on the
#       form (the response itself never leaves the server);
#    3. verify(id, input) compares the input to the expected response, then
#       OUBLIE this CAPTCHA: each image is used only once, so a bot cannot
#       reuse a response that has already been found.
#
# A single object CaptchaService for the entire server, used by multiple
# requests EN PARALLÈLE (the server processes them across multiple threads): a
# lock ensures that only one thread at a time reads from or modifies the
# dictionary of pending CAPTCHAs.
#
# Assumed limitation: the memory of a single process. With multiple processes
# or multiple servers, shared storage would be required.
# =========================================================================
import secrets
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from threading import Lock

from rdvmedecins.auth import dessin_captcha

# Image validity period: you have 10 minutes to fill out the form
DUREE_VIE = timedelta(minutes=10)

# Memory safeguard: after that, all pending CAPTCHAs are discarded
MAX_CAPTCHAS = 10_000


# A CAPTCHA: ID, to be placed in the hidden field "captchaId" on the form;
# SVG, the image, to be inserted as-is into the page
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Captcha:
    id: str
    svg: str


class CaptchaService:

    def __init__(self):
         # id -> (expected response, expiration date)
        self._en_attente: dict[str, tuple[str, datetime]] = {}
        self._verrou = Lock()

    def generer(self) -> Captcha:
        texte = dessin_captcha.texte_aleatoire(5)  # 5 characters
        id = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)  # a random identifier that cannot be guessed
        with self._verrou:
            self._purger()
            self._en_attente[id] = (texte, datetime.now() + DUREE_VIE)
        return Captcha(id, dessin_captcha.svg(texte))

     # true if [saisie] is the correct answer to the CAPTCHA [id] (regardless of
     # capital letters). The CAPTCHA is consumed in all cases: if two
     # requests present the same captcha at the same time, only one
     # will be removed (popped, under the lock)—the other will fail.
    def verifier(self, id: str | None, saisie: str | None) -> bool:
        with self._verrou:
            attendu = self._en_attente.pop(id, None) if id else None
        if attendu is None or saisie is None:
            return False
        texte, expire = attendu
        return expire > datetime.now() and texte.lower() == saisie.strip().lower()

     # (called under the lock)
    def _purger(self):
        maintenant = datetime.now()
        for id in [id for id, (_, expire) in self._en_attente.items() if expire <= maintenant]:
            del self._en_attente[id]
        if len(self._en_attente) >= MAX_CAPTCHAS:
            self._en_attente.clear()

The service from Example 27, with an addition: the [_purger] method (lines 77–82), called each time a CAPTCHA is created, discards expired CAPTCHAs. Without it, captchas that are displayed but never used (such as when a login page is opened and then abandoned) would accumulate in memory. [MAX_CAPTCHAS] acts as a safeguard: a bot requesting millions of login pages would not be able to exhaust the server’s memory. The number [10_000] is written with an underscore, which separates the thousands for readability ([Python] ignores this). The list of identifiers to be deleted is constructed before the deletion loop: you cannot delete keys from a dictionary while iterating through it.

docs.title: 11.13.7. auth/limiteur.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# auth/limiteur.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Second line of defense against bots (the first is the CAPTCHA): COMPTE
# attempts, and once a threshold is exceeded, BLOQUE for a while.
#
#    - Login: after LOGIN_MAX_ECHECS failed attempts (incorrect CAPTCHA or incorrect
#      password) for the same login from the same IP address IP, this pair
#      is blocked for LOGIN_BLOCAGE_MINUTES minutes. The same IP address IP is also
#      blocked if it accumulates 5 times as many failed attempts, across all logins (a
#      bot that tries thousands of different logins);
#    - account creation: no more than INSCRIPTION_MAX_PAR_HEURE accounts created
#      per hour from the same address IP.
#
# Caution in the classroom: all computers frequently access the Internet
# via the MÊME address IP. This is why the connection block applies
# primarily on the pair (IP, login)—a student who enters the wrong password
# does not block their neighbors—and why the thresholds are adjustable
# in config.py.
#
# A single object for the entire server, called by parallel requests:
# all public methods acquire the lock—a single thread at a
# time reads ET and updates the counters.
# =========================================================================
import math
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from threading import Lock

UNE_HEURE = timedelta(hours=1)


class Compteur:
    def __init__(self, debut: datetime):
        self.nombre = 0  # Attempts counted within the current window
        self.debut = debut  # start of the counting window
        self.bloque_jusqua = datetime.min  # datetime.min if not blocked


class LimiteurTentatives:

    def __init__(self, login_max_echecs: int, login_blocage_minutes: int,
                 inscription_max_par_heure: int):
        self._compteurs: dict[str, Compteur] = {}
        self._verrou = Lock()
        self._max_echecs_login = login_max_echecs
        self._duree_blocage_login = timedelta(minutes=login_blocage_minutes)
        self._max_inscriptions = inscription_max_par_heure

     # ---------------------------------------------------------------- connection

     # number of remaining minutes of lockout (0 = attempt is allowed)
    def minutes_blocage_login(self, ip: str, login: str) -> int:
        with self._verrou:
            return max(self._minutes_restantes(self._cle_login(ip, login)),
                       self._minutes_restantes(self._cle_ip(ip)))

    def echec_login(self, ip: str, login: str):
        with self._verrou:
            self._compter(self._cle_login(ip, login), self._max_echecs_login,
                          self._duree_blocage_login, self._duree_blocage_login)
            self._compter(self._cle_ip(ip), self._max_echecs_login * 5,
                          self._duree_blocage_login, self._duree_blocage_login)

     # A successful login resets the CE login counter
    def reussite_login(self, ip: str, login: str):
        with self._verrou:
            self._compteurs.pop(self._cle_login(ip, login), None)

     # ---------------------------------------------------------------- registration

    def minutes_blocage_inscription(self, ip: str) -> int:
        with self._verrou:
            return self._minutes_restantes(f"inscription|{ip}")

     # one-hour window; once the quota is reached, access is blocked until the end of the hour
    def inscription_reussie(self, ip: str):
        with self._verrou:
            self._compter(f"inscription|{ip}", self._max_inscriptions, UNE_HEURE, UNE_HEURE)

     # ---------------------------------------------------------------- common mechanism
     # (private methods are always called under a lock)

    def _minutes_restantes(self, cle: str) -> int:
        compteur = self._compteurs.get(cle)
        if compteur is None:
            return 0
        reste = (compteur.bloque_jusqua - datetime.now()).total_seconds()
         # rounded to the nearest minute SUPÉRIEURE: 30 seconds of blocking time remaining -> "1 minute"
        return max(0, math.ceil(reste / 60))

     # counts one attempt; if the threshold is reached within the window, locks
    def _compter(self, cle: str, maximum: int, fenetre: timedelta, blocage: timedelta):
        maintenant = datetime.now()
        self._purger(maintenant)
        compteur = self._compteurs.get(cle)
        if compteur is None or maintenant - compteur.debut > fenetre:
            compteur = Compteur(maintenant)
            self._compteurs[cle] = compteur
        compteur.nombre += 1
        if compteur.nombre >= maximum:
            compteur.bloque_jusqua = maintenant + blocage
            compteur.nombre = 0  # After the lock, the counter resets to zero
            compteur.debut = compteur.bloque_jusqua

     # Counters that are no longer in use (neither blocked nor recent) are ignored
    def _purger(self, maintenant: datetime):
        if len(self._compteurs) < 1000:
            return
        for cle in [cle for cle, c in self._compteurs.items()
                    if c.bloque_jusqua < maintenant and maintenant - c.debut > UNE_HEURE]:
            del self._compteurs[cle]

    @staticmethod
    def _cle_login(ip: str, login: str) -> str:
        return f"login|{ip}|{login.strip().lower()}"

    @staticmethod
    def _cle_ip(ip: str) -> str:
        return f"ip|{ip}"

A more complete version of the limiter from Example 27:

  • The connection block first targets the pair (address IP, login): in a classroom, all computers often access the Internet through the same address, IP, and a student who enters the wrong password should not block their neighbors. However, an address is also blocked if it accumulates five times as many failed attempts, across all logins: this is the case for a bot that tries thousands of different logins (lines 57–61);
  • account creation is limited to a certain number of accounts per hour per IP address (lines 71–78);
  • The counters are stored in a single dictionary, under keys prefixed by their usage ([login|...], [ip|...], [inscription|...]);
  • lines 92–103: A counter tracks attempts within a time window; an attempt that occurs after the window ends triggers a new one. When the threshold is reached, the key is locked, and the counter resets to zero;
  • lines 106–111: Once the counter exceeds 1,000 entries, those that are no longer in use (neither blocked nor recent) are discarded.

Like the CAPTCHA, the limiter stores its data in the process’s memory: this is acceptable for an application served by a single process (the development server, [Waitress]), but not for multiple processes or multiple servers, which would not share their counters (shared storage would then be required, such as [Redis]).

docs.title: 11.13.8. auth/passe_inscription.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# auth/passe_inscription.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The "pass" for creating an account.
#
# To open the “Create a Customer Account” page, you must first have
# entered the CAPTCHA from the authentication page (see
# controllers/inscription.py, POST /registration/access). The server returns
# then issues a token:
#    - a random identifier, stored in a cookie named HttpOnly;
#    - valid for 15 minutes (enough time to fill out the form, even if you
#      trying multiple times after data entry errors);
#    - expires as soon as an account is created: UN captcha solved = UN account
#      . A bot cannot create accounts in bulk.
#
# Without a valid passcode, GET and POST /registration redirect to the
# authentication page: typing URL /registration directly does not allow
# bypass the CAPTCHA.
#
# Like the CAPTCHA, the tokens reside in the process’s memory.
# =========================================================================
import secrets
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from threading import Lock

from flask import Response

COOKIE = "rdvmedecins_inscription"

DUREE_VIE = timedelta(minutes=15)
MAX_PASSES = 10_000


class PasseInscription:

    def __init__(self):
         # ID -> expiration date
        self._passes: dict[str, datetime] = {}
        self._verrou = Lock()

     # Issues a new token; returns its ID
    def emettre(self) -> str:
        id = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)
        with self._verrou:
            self._purger()
            self._passes[id] = datetime.now() + DUREE_VIE
        return id

     # true if [id] is an existing, unexpired token
    def est_valide(self, id: str | None) -> bool:
        with self._verrou:
            expire = self._passes.get(id) if id else None
        return expire is not None and expire > datetime.now()

     # the pass has been used: discard it
    def consommer(self, id: str | None):
        with self._verrou:
            self._passes.pop(id, None)

     # (called under a lock)
    def _purger(self):
        maintenant = datetime.now()
        for id in [id for id, expire in self._passes.items() if expire <= maintenant]:
            del self._passes[id]
        if len(self._passes) >= MAX_PASSES:
            self._passes.clear()


# the cookie is sent by the browser only to the /registration... addresses
def deposer_cookie(reponse: Response, id: str, secure: bool):
    reponse.set_cookie(COOKIE, id, max_age=DUREE_VIE, path="/inscription", httponly=True,
                       samesite="Lax", secure=secure)


# ... and it is cleared by resetting it to empty, with a lifetime of zero
def effacer_cookie(reponse: Response):
    reponse.delete_cookie(COOKIE, path="/inscription")

Creating a customer account is a public page: a bot could create accounts in bulk. It is therefore protected by the login page’s CAPTCHA: the “Create a Customer Account” button sends this CAPTCHA to the server, which, if it is correct, issues a token:

  • lines 42–47: a random identifier, valid for 15 minutes, stored in memory like the CAPTCHAs;
  • lines 50–53: The registration page verifies the pass for each request—GET is treated the same as POST;
  • lines 56–58: Creating an account consumes the pass: one solved CAPTCHA equals one account at most;
  • lines 70–72: The pass is stored in a cookie. Its attribute, [path="/inscription"], limits the requests to which the browser attaches it: only addresses beginning with [/inscription];
  • lines 76–77: To delete a cookie, you must specify the same path as when it was set.

docs.title: 11.13.9. controllers/auth.py
docs.text:
The connection controller, which uses all of these services.

# =========================================================================
# controllers/auth.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The routes PUBLIQUES for the connection:
#    GE T         / redirects to the role’s home page (or to /login)
#    GE T /log  in displays the login form (with its CAPTCHA)
#    POST /logi  n checks attempt limit, CAPTCHA, username/password
#    POST /logou t logs out
#
# Protection against bots, in this order:
#    1. Too many recent failed attempts for this login from this address IP?
#       -> immediate rejection, without even checking the password;
#    2. Incorrect CAPTCHA answer? -> Denied (counted as a failed attempt);
#    3. Only then is the password verified.
# The password for a rejected attempt is not verified in steps
# 1 or 2: a bot therefore cannot learn anything by persisting.
# =========================================================================
from flask import Blueprint, g, redirect, render_template, request, url_for

from rdvmedecins.auth.auth_service import AuthService
from rdvmedecins.auth.securite import publique
from rdvmedecins.entities import Role
from rdvmedecins.models.modeles_vues import LoginModele, Message
from rdvmedecins.web.services import auth_service, captchas, limiteur

auth = Blueprint("auth", __name__)


# the home page for each role, immediately after logging in
def page_accueil(role: Role) -> str:
    return url_for("espace.espace_patient") if role == Role.USER else url_for("agenda.afficher")


# the visitor’s address IP. Behind a reverse proxy (nginx...), this would be
# the proxy’s address: the application would then need to be wrapped in the
# Werkzeug’s ProxyFix middleware, which reads the X-Forwarded-For header.
def adresse_ip() -> str:
    return request.remote_addr or ""


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /
# The route is public: the user, if any, was identified by
# auth/securite.py (g.utilisateur), but nothing is required.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@auth.get("/")
@publique
def accueil():
    return redirect(page_accueil(g.utilisateur.role) if g.utilisateur else url_for("auth.afficher_login"))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /login[?login=xxx]: the optional parameter pre-fills the
# login (used immediately after creating an account; see controllers/inscription.py)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@auth.get("/login")
@publique
def afficher_login():
     # already logged in (token still valid): goes directly to the home page
    if g.utilisateur:
        return redirect(page_accueil(g.utilisateur.role))
    return formulaire(request.args.get("login", "")[:30], None)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /login
# request.form.get: a missing field returns "None" (not a 400 error) -
# the code determines what to do with it.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@auth.post("/login")
@publique
def se_connecter():
    login = (request.form.get("login") or "").strip()
    password = request.form.get("password") or ""
    ip = adresse_ip()

     # 1. Too many recent failures?
    minutes = limiteur().minutes_blocage_login(ip, login)
    if minutes > 0:
        return formulaire(login, Message("ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS", {"minutes": str(minutes)}))

     # 2. The CAPTCHA
    if not captchas().verifier(request.form.get("captchaId"), request.form.get("captcha")):
        limiteur().echec_login(ip, login)
        return formulaire(login, Message("ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA"))

     # 3. the password
    user = auth_service().valider_utilisateur(login, password) if login and password else None
    if user is None:
        limiteur().echec_login(ip, login)
        return formulaire(login, Message("LOGIN.ERROR"))

    limiteur().reussite_login(ip, login)
    reponse = redirect(page_accueil(user.role))
    auth_service().deposer_jeton(reponse, user)
    return reponse


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /logout: clear the token cookie, then go to the
# login page. POST only: a simple link (GET), placed on another site,
# cannot log the user out without their knowledge.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@auth.post("/logout")
@publique
def se_deconnecter():
    reponse = redirect(url_for("auth.afficher_login"))
    AuthService.effacer_jeton(reponse)
    return reponse


# the form, always with a NOUVEAU CAPTCHA (each image is used
# only once); the entered username is displayed again, but never the password
def formulaire(login: str, erreur: Message | None):
    modele = LoginModele("LOGIN.TITLE", erreur, login, captchas().generer())
    return render_template("login.html", modele=modele)
  • line 24: Shared services are obtained through small functions in the [web/services.py] module (discussed later), which retrieve them from [app.extensions];
  • lines 30–31: Each role has its own home page: a patient portal for patients, and the calendar for others;
  • lines 37–38: the visitor’s address IP. Behind a reverse proxy ([nginx], [Apache]), this would be the proxy’s address, which is the same for all visitors: the application would then need to be wrapped in the [ProxyFix] middleware from [Werkzeug] (see the chapter on the lifecycle), which reads the original address from the [X-Forwarded-For] header added by the proxy;
  • lines 46–49: the public root of the site: it redirects to the user’s home page or to the login page;
  • lines 56–62: the login page. A user who is already logged in (whose token is still valid) is sent directly to their home page. The optional parameter [login] pre-fills the field (after an account is created); [[:30]] limits its length to that of a username;
  • Lines 70–96: the login process, in three steps, in this order: potential blocking, the CAPTCHA, and then only the password. An attempt rejected in the first two steps never checks the password: a bot cannot learn anything by persisting. [request.form.get(...) or ""]: an empty field returns an empty string. The error message is an object [Message]: a translation key and its parameters (discussed later);
  • lines 104–109: logout, in POST (example 25). It is public: a user whose session has expired must be able to click “Log Out” without first being redirected;
  • lines 114–116: the login page, still with a new CAPTCHA. Its template is a [LoginModele] object (see [models/modeles_vues.py]).

Note that the login form does not use [WTForms]: its three fields have no validation rules (an empty username simply results in a failed login), and the form is protected against CSRF attacks by [CSRFProtect], like all forms in the application.

docs.title: 11.14. The Web Layer: Shared Services
docs.text: The [web] folder contains what the controllers have in common. Each module in it answers a question that all controllers ask themselves: how to obtain a service, translate a text, display a message after a redirect, redisplay a rejected form, or convert an error into a page.

docs.title: 11.14.1. web/services.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/services.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The application’s shared objects (see Example 06): they are created UNE
# times by the application factory (rdvmedecins/__init__.py), and
# stored in the dictionary app.extensions. These small functions
# are retrieved by the application processing the current request
# (current_app); they also provide their TYPE to the analysis tools.
# =========================================================================
from flask import current_app

from rdvmedecins.auth.auth_service import AuthService
from rdvmedecins.auth.captcha import CaptchaService
from rdvmedecins.auth.limiteur import LimiteurTentatives
from rdvmedecins.auth.passe_inscription import PasseInscription
from rdvmedecins.web.application_model import ApplicationModel


def application() -> ApplicationModel:
    return current_app.extensions["rdvmedecins.application"]


def auth_service() -> AuthService:
    return current_app.extensions["rdvmedecins.auth"]


def captchas() -> CaptchaService:
    return current_app.extensions["rdvmedecins.captchas"]


def limiteur() -> LimiteurTentatives:
    return current_app.extensions["rdvmedecins.limiteur"]


def passes() -> PasseInscription:
    return current_app.extensions["rdvmedecins.passes"]

The shared objects, created by the factory and stored in [app.extensions], are retrieved by these small functions (example 06). They eliminate the need to repeat the dictionary key in each controller and provide their type to analysis tools: in a controller, the editor knows that [application()] is a [ApplicationModel] and offers its methods.

docs.title: 11.14.2. web/traducteur.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/traducteur.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# French/English translation of the interface (see example 22).
#
# The dictionaries are the MÊMES files, which are the same as those in the NestJS versions,
# ASP.NET Core and Spring MVC components of the application (i18n/fr.json, i18n/en.json),
# read only once at startup.
#
# In the views, the t function (see web/modele_commun.py):
#    {{ t("LOGIN.TITLE") }                           } without parameters;
#    {{ t("ESPACE.HELLO", name=modele.patient)       }} named parameters;
#    {{ t(message.cle, message.parametres) }         } a dictionary of parameters.
#
# LA LANGUE COURANTE: g.langue, set for each request based on a cookie
# (see rdvmedecins/__init__.py, function fixer_langue).
# =========================================================================
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

from flask import g

LANGUES = ("fr", "en")
LANGUE_PAR_DEFAUT = "fr"

# the cookie that stores the selected language (see controllers/langue.py)
COOKIE_LANGUE = "rdvmedecins_langue"

# {name}: a parameter in a text
PARAMETRE = re.compile(r"\{(\w+)\}")


# the supported language corresponding to [code]: "en" -> "en"; "de" or None -> "fr"
def langue(code: str | None) -> str:
    return code if code in LANGUES else LANGUE_PAR_DEFAUT


class Traducteur:

    def __init__(self, dossier: Path):
         # language -> (full key "LOGIN.TITLE" -> text)
        self._dictionnaires: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
        for code in LANGUES:
            with open(dossier / f"{code}.json", encoding="utf-8") as fichier:
                self._dictionnaires[code] = self._aplatir(json.load(fichier))

    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
     # translate("MEDECINS.ADDED", {"name": "Marie PELISSIER"})
        # -> searches for "MEDECINS.ADDED" in the language dictionary, and
           # replaces {name} with its value. A key missing from the requested language
           # is looked up in French; if it is missing everywhere, the key
           # itself is displayed (this immediately highlights an omission).
     # Parameters: a dictionary and/or named parameters.
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------------
    def traduire(self, cle: str | None, parametres: dict | None = None, **autres) -> str:
        if not cle:
            return ""
        texte = self._dictionnaires[langue(g.get("langue"))].get(cle)
        if texte is None:
            texte = self._dictionnaires[LANGUE_PAR_DEFAUT].get(cle, cle)
        valeurs = {**(parametres or {}), **autres}
        if not valeurs:
            return texte
        return PARAMETRE.sub(lambda m: str(valeurs.get(m.group(1), m.group(0))), texte)

     # { "LOGIN": { "TITLE": "Login" } } -> { "LOGIN.TITLE": "Login" }
    @classmethod
    def _aplatir(cls, noeud: dict, prefixe: str = "") -> dict[str, str]:
        resultat = {}
        for cle, valeur in noeud.items():
            cle_complete = f"{prefixe}.{cle}" if prefixe else cle
            if isinstance(valeur, dict):
                resultat.update(cls._aplatir(valeur, cle_complete))
            else:
                resultat[cle_complete] = valeur
        return resultat

The translator from Example 22, with three additions:

  • Lines 56–65: A text’s parameters can be provided by a dictionary (the second parameter, [parametres]), by named parameters ([**autres]), or both. Application messages (the [Message] class, discussed later) carry their parameters in a dictionary; views, on the other hand, prefer named parameters. [{**a, **b}] creates a dictionary that combines those from [a] and [b];
  • line 61: a key missing from the requested language is looked up in French before being displayed as-is;
  • line 59: [g.get("langue")] returns [None] if [g] lacks the [langue] attribute, rather than throwing an exception: the translator works even if an error occurs before the [before_request] function, which sets the language.

The name of the language cookie is prefixed with the application name ([rdvmedecins_langue]), just like the token and pass: cookies are associated with a domain name ([localhost]), not a port. The examples, which are also served by [localhost], could otherwise read the application’s cookies.

docs.title: 11.14.3. web/modele_commun.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/modele_commun.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What TOUTES views need, regardless of the page (see example
# 15): a "context processor," executed before each
# view, adds its variables to the template for all views:
#    - user: the logged-in user (or None), for the navigation bar;
#    - langu     age: "fr" or "en";
#    - path       : the requested URL (active menu item in the navigation bar,
#                    "Other image" link in the CAPTCHA);
#    -           t : the translation function (see web/traducteur.py).
# Flash messages, on the other hand, are read by the template (get_flashed_messages).
# =========================================================================
from flask import g, request

from rdvmedecins.web.traducteur import Traducteur


def enregistrer(app, traducteur: Traducteur):

    @app.context_processor
    def modele_commun():
        return {
            "utilisateur": g.get("utilisateur"),
            "langue": g.get("langue", "fr"),
            "chemin": request.path,
            "t": traducteur.traduire,
        }

The context processor from Example 15: four variables available in all views, without actions having to provide them: the logged-in user (for the navigation bar), the language (for the page’s [lang] attribute and the FR / EN buttons), the path of the requested URL (for the active menu and the “Other image” link in the CAPTCHA), and the translation function [t]. [g.get("utilisateur")] returns [None] if the attribute does not exist (for example, a fabricated error page before authentication).

docs.title: 11.14.4. web/flash.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/flash.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# "Flash" messages: a message to be displayed UNE times on the page
# SUIVANTE (see Example 20). This is the natural complement to the
# "Post / Redirect / Get" pattern used by all forms in the application:
# A successful POST does not generate a page; it redirects (302) to a page
# GET; the message itself must survive the redirect.
#
# Flask stores them in SESSION, that is, in a SIGNÉ cookie via the
# secret key (SECRET_KEY): the server remains SANS ÉTAT; it does not store anything in
# between requests. The browser can read this cookie (it is
# not encrypted), but it cannot modify it without the signature giving it away.
#
# A message does not contain text, but rather a CLÉ translation and its
# settings: it is translated when displayed, into the language of
# the page (see templates/layout.html). Its category: "success" (displayed at the
# the top of the page) or “danger” (an error, displayed at the bottom).
# =========================================================================
from flask import flash


def flash_succes(cle: str, **parametres):
    flash({"cle": cle, "parametres": parametres}, "success")


def flash_erreur(cle: str, **parametres):
    flash({"cle": cle, "parametres": parametres}, "danger")

The flash messages from Example 20. A message is not text, but a dictionary: the translation key and its parameters. It will be translated at the time of display, by the template, into the page’s language. [Flask] stores the messages in the session, which is a cookie: to do this, it converts them to JSON, which accepts a dictionary of strings. The message category ([success] or [danger], the color names from [Bootstrap]) determines its location: at the top of the page for a success, at the bottom for an error.

docs.title: 11.14.5. web/erreurs.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/erreurs.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# How errors become pages HTML. Three administrators
# share the work (see Example 24):
#
#    1. a SessionInvalide (account deleted since login) -> return to
#       the login page, as with an expired session;
#    2. an error HTTP: abort(400), abort(403) (insufficient role), page
#       unknown (404), unsupported method (405), missing or invalid anti-CSRF token
#       missing or invalid (400)... -> the error page, with the original code;
#    3. any other exception (a true anomaly) -> logged
#       with its call stack; the user sees the
#       500 error page—never the call stack.
# =========================================================================
from flask import current_app, redirect, render_template, url_for
from werkzeug.exceptions import HTTPException

from rdvmedecins.auth.auth_service import AuthService
from rdvmedecins.auth.securite import SessionInvalide
from rdvmedecins.models.modeles_vues import ErreurModele
from rdvmedecins.web.flash import flash_erreur

MESSAGES = {
    400: "ERRORS.BAD_REQUEST",
    403: "ERRORS.FORBIDDEN",
    404: "ERRORS.NOT_FOUND",
}


def page_erreur(code: int):
    modele = ErreurModele("ERROR_PAGE.TITLE", None, code, MESSAGES.get(code, "ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR"))
     # The page retains the error code (404 remains 404...)
    return render_template("erreur.html", modele=modele), code


def enregistrer(app):

    @app.errorhandler(SessionInvalide)
    def session_invalide(e):
        reponse = redirect(url_for("auth.afficher_login"))
        AuthService.effacer_jeton(reponse)
        flash_erreur("ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED")
        return reponse

    @app.errorhandler(HTTPException)
    def erreur_http(e: HTTPException):
        return page_erreur(e.code or 500)

     # Exception: the parent class of all exceptions; this handler
     # only receives exceptions that no more specific handler has handled
    @app.errorhandler(Exception)
    def anomalie(e: Exception):
        current_app.logger.exception("erreur inattendue")
        return page_erreur(500)

The error handlers in Example 24:

  • lines 31–34: the error page, with the original error code (a 404 page remains a 404 response) and a translated message chosen based on the code;
  • lines 39–44: an account deleted since login: redirect to the login page, as with an expired session;
  • lines 46–48: all HTTP errors: [abort(403)], an unknown page (404), a forbidden method (405), a missing or invalid anti-CSRF token (400, handled by [CSRFProtect])...;
  • lines 52–55: any other exception, i.e., a true anomaly (a programming error, a database that has become inaccessible). [current_app.logger] is the application log (an object of the standard module [logging]); its method [exception] writes the message to it, followed by the call stack of the current exception. The user, however, sees only the 500 error page: never the call stack, which would reveal internal details of the application. [Flask] always selects the most specific handler: a HTTP error is handled by the second handler, not by this one.

docs.title: 11.14.6. web/application_model.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/application_model.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The cache/facade of the business layer (the equivalent of the class
# [ApplicationModel] in previous versions of the application): the
# lists of doctors and clients are read once at startup, then
# retrieved from memory.
#
# These lists can be CHANGER (the ADMIN adds, modifies, or deletes
# doctors and clients): every write operation therefore goes through this facade,
# which then updates the relevant list immediately afterward. This is the whole point of a
# entry point UNIQUE to the business layer: the rule “update =>
# cache reload” is implemented only here.
#
# A single object for the entire application, used by
# processed by EN PARALLÈLE, across multiple threads. Therefore, we never modify
# a list in place: the entire list is REMPLACE replaced with a new one. In Python,
# assigning a value to an attribute is atomic: a thread reading the list sees
# either the old or the new one, never a list that’s halfway constructed.
# =========================================================================
from datetime import date

from rdvmedecins.domain.agenda import AgendaMedecinJour
from rdvmedecins.entities import Client, Creneau, Medecin, Rv
from rdvmedecins.metier.donnees import DonneesPersonne
from rdvmedecins.metier.metier import Metier


# same contract as the business layer (Metier)
class ApplicationModel:

    def __init__(self, metier: Metier):
        self._metier = metier
         # Initial loading of both lists upon application startup.
         # A read error (database inaccessible...) is not caught:
         # It shuts down the server rather than letting it start "from scratch"
        self._medecins: list[Medecin] = []
        self._clients: list[Client] = []
        self._recharger_medecins()
        self._recharger_clients()

    def _recharger_medecins(self):
        self._medecins = list(self._metier.get_all_medecins())

    def _recharger_clients(self):
        self._clients = list(self._metier.get_all_clients())

     # ------------------------------------------------ reads from the cache

    def get_all_medecins(self) -> list[Medecin]:
        return self._medecins

    def get_all_clients(self) -> list[Client]:
        return self._clients

     # the doctor whose user account is [id_user]—is used for preselection,
     # for a logged-in doctor, their own calendar
    def get_medecin_by_user_id(self, id_user: int) -> Medecin | None:
        return next((m for m in self._medecins if m.id_user == id_user), None)

     # ------------------------------------------------ simple delegations

    def get_all_creneaux(self, id_medecin: int) -> list[Creneau]:
        return self._metier.get_all_creneaux(id_medecin)

    def get_rv_medecin_jour(self, id_medecin: int, jour: date) -> list[Rv]:
        return self._metier.get_rv_medecin_jour(id_medecin, jour)

    def get_client_by_id(self, id: int) -> Client | None:
        return self._metier.get_client_by_id(id)

    def get_medecin_by_id(self, id: int) -> Medecin | None:
        return self._metier.get_medecin_by_id(id)

    def get_rv_by_id(self, id: int) -> Rv | None:
        return self._metier.get_rv_by_id(id)

    def get_creneau_by_id(self, id: int) -> Creneau | None:
        return self._metier.get_creneau_by_id(id)

    def get_agenda_medecin_jour(self, id_medecin: int, jour: date) -> AgendaMedecinJour | None:
        return self._metier.get_agenda_medecin_jour(id_medecin, jour)

     # no cache here: the most recent data is what counts (a patient
     # who has just modified or deleted their account)
    def get_client_by_user_id(self, id_user: int) -> Client | None:
        return self._metier.get_client_by_user_id(id_user)

    def get_rv_a_venir_client(self, id_client: int) -> list[Rv]:
        return self._metier.get_rv_a_venir_client(id_client)

    def ajouter_rv(self, jour: date, creneau: Creneau, client: Client) -> Rv:
        return self._metier.ajouter_rv(jour, creneau, client)

    def supprimer_rv(self, rv: Rv) -> None:
        self._metier.supprimer_rv(rv)

     # ------------------------------------------------ entries => reload

    def ajouter_medecin(self, donnees: DonneesPersonne) -> Medecin:
        medecin = self._metier.ajouter_medecin(donnees)
        self._recharger_medecins()
        return medecin

    def modifier_medecin(self, id: int, donnees: DonneesPersonne) -> Medecin:
        medecin = self._metier.modifier_medecin(id, donnees)
        self._recharger_medecins()
        return medecin

    def supprimer_medecin(self, id: int) -> None:
        self._metier.supprimer_medecin(id)
        self._recharger_medecins()

    def ajouter_client(self, donnees: DonneesPersonne) -> Client:
        client = self._metier.ajouter_client(donnees)
        self._recharger_clients()
        return client

    def modifier_client(self, id: int, donnees: DonneesPersonne) -> Client:
        client = self._metier.modifier_client(id, donnees)
        self._recharger_clients()
        return client

    def supprimer_client(self, id: int) -> None:
        self._metier.supprimer_client(id)
        self._recharger_clients()

The web layer cache and its interface to the business layer:

  • lines 32–40: the lists of doctors and patients are read once, at startup. They are used every time the calendar is displayed (the drop-down list of doctors, the list of patients): keeping them in memory avoids two SQL requests per page. A read error is not caught: it causes the application to crash at startup (see “Common Problems”);
  • lines 50–59: data retrieved from the cache. [get_medecin_by_user_id] identifies the logged-in doctor to preselect their own calendar;
  • lines 63–96: the other read operations, and the appointments, are simply relayed to the business layer. [get_client_by_user_id] does not use the cache: a patient who has just modified or deleted their account must see the most recent data;
  • lines 100–126: Each update to doctors or clients refreshes the relevant list. This is the benefit of a single entry point to the business layer: the rule “update, then refresh the cache” is implemented only here.

This unique object is used by requests processed in parallel across multiple threads: therefore, a list is never modified in place (by [append] or [remove]); instead, it is replaced entirely with a new one. In [Python], assigning an attribute is atomic: a thread reading the list sees either the old or the new version, never a partially constructed list. Therefore, no lock is needed.

[ApplicationModel] adheres to the [Metier] contract (it has the same methods as [MetierService]): for the controllers, it is the business layer. We could remove the cache without touching the controllers by directly placing [MetierService] inside [app.extensions].

docs.title: 11.14.7. web/validation.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/validation.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What’s needed for a rejected form: the errors in
# field-by-field, and the fields to be highlighted in red.
# =========================================================================
from flask_wtf import FlaskForm

from rdvmedecins.models.modeles_vues import EtatFormulaire, Message


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# the validated form (see forms/formulaires.py) -> the dictionary
# field -> message key, keeping only the first message from each
# field: { "name": "ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED", ... }
#
# Our messages are translation keys ("ERRORS...."). A message that
# WTForms wrote himself (in English) is replaced by the key
# ERRORS.INVALID_FORM.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def erreurs_de(form: FlaskForm) -> dict[str, str]:
    erreurs = {}
    for champ, messages in form.errors.items():
        message = str(messages[0])
        erreurs[champ] = message if message.startswith("ERRORS.") else "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM"
    return erreurs


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# the form fields affected by each business "data entry" error
# (a duplicate): they are highlighted in red, with the message at the bottom of the page
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER = {
    "ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN": ["login"],
    "ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS": ["prenom", "nom"],
    "ERRORS.PATIENT_ALREADY_EXISTS": ["prenom", "nom"],
}


# the status of a form to be (re)displayed: a message below each field
# rejected by validation (errors), and the fields to be highlighted in red,
# these and any others (autres_champs)
def etat(erreurs: dict[str, str], autres_champs: list[str] | None = None) -> EtatFormulaire:
    return EtatFormulaire(dict(erreurs), set(erreurs) | set(autres_champs or []))


# LE page error message, displayed at the bottom of the page: [erreur] if
# there is one, otherwise "The form contains errors." if there are
# field errors, otherwise nothing
def message_page(erreurs: dict[str, str], erreur: Message | None) -> Message | None:
    if erreur is not None:
        return erreur
    return Message("ERRORS.INVALID_FORM") if erreurs else None

What is needed to redisplay a rejected form:

  • lines 21–26: the errors from a [WTForms] form (example 19), in the form of a “field → message key” dictionary, keeping only the first message for each field. The messages from our validators are translation keys ([ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED], see [forms/formulaires.py]); a message that [WTForms] would have generated itself, in English, is replaced by a generic key;
  • lines 33–36: Some business-logic errors pertain to specific fields—such as a username that’s already taken or a name with the same spelling. Their error messages appear at the bottom of the page, but the affected fields are highlighted in red so the user can immediately see what to correct (see the screenshot of the name with the same spelling above);
  • lines 43–44: the state of a form to be redisplayed: the messages below the fields, and all fields to be highlighted in red. [set(erreurs)] is the set of keys in the dictionary; the operator [|] performs a union of two sets;
  • lines 50–53: the general footer message.

docs.title: 11.14.8. web/outils.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# web/outils.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Small utility functions in the web layer:
#    - labels: "Ms. Alice DURAND";
#    - dates: "yyyy-mm-dd", times "8:05", days "Wednesday, September 23, 2026";
#    - input: reading a positive integer sent by the browser;
#    - user: the logged-in user and their patient (Client entity).
# =========================================================================
import re
from datetime import date, datetime

from babel.dates import format_date
from flask import g

from rdvmedecins.auth.securite import SessionInvalide
from rdvmedecins.auth.utilisateur import UtilisateurConnecte
from rdvmedecins.entities import Client, Creneau, Personne

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- labels


# "Ms. Alice DURAND"
def libelle(p: Personne) -> str:
    return f"{p.titre} {p.prenom} {p.nom}"


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- dates

# the date format in URL and in the <input type="date"> field
FORMAT_ISO = re.compile(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}")


# the date, if [texte] is a valid date in the yyyy-mm-dd format; None otherwise.
# strptime checks that the date exists: "2026-02-30" is rejected
def date_valide(texte: str | None) -> date | None:
    if texte is None or not FORMAT_ISO.fullmatch(texte):
        return None
    try:
        return datetime.strptime(texte, "%Y-%m-%d").date()
    except ValueError:
        return None


def iso(jour: date) -> str:
    return jour.isoformat()


# "8:05" rather than "8:5"
def formater_heure(h: int, m: int) -> str:
    return f"{h}:{m:02d}"


def horaire(c: Creneau) -> str:
    return f"{formater_heure(c.hdebut, c.mdebut)} - {formater_heure(c.hfin, c.mfin)}"


# "Wednesday, September 23, 2026" / "Wednesday 23 September 2026," depending on the
# language of the request (g.langue). The Babel format: EEEE the day of the
# the week spelled out, d the day, MMMM the month spelled out, y the year
def formater_jour(jour: date) -> str:
    return format_date(jour, "EEEE d MMMM y", locale=g.langue)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- input


# "3" -> 3; "", "abc", "-2", "+2", None -> None
def entier_positif(valeur: str | None) -> int | None:
    if valeur is None or not re.fullmatch(r"\d{1,9}", valeur):
        return None
    n = int(valeur)
    return n if n > 0 else None


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- user


# the logged-in user (see auth/securite.py). Protected actions are
# are called only if it exists; as a precaution, its absence is treated
# as an expired session.
def utilisateur() -> UtilisateurConnecte:
    if g.utilisateur is None:
        raise SessionInvalide()
    return g.utilisateur


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# The patient (Client entity) that corresponds to the logged-in user.
#
# The token JWT contains only the ID of COMPTE (users.id). For a role
# For USER, the corresponding client is identified using the clients.user column.
#
# If there is no match, it means the account was deleted since the
# login, even though its token is still valid: it is treated as a
# expired session (see SessionInvalide).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def patient_connecte(application) -> Client:
    patient = application.get_client_by_user_id(utilisateur().user_id)
    if patient is None:
        raise SessionInvalide()
    return patient

Utility functions used by multiple controllers:

  • line 24: a person’s title, “Ms. Alice DURAND”;
  • lines 31–42: parsing a date in the [aaaa-mm-jj] format, which is the same as that used for the URL entries in the calendar ([jour=2026-09-26]) and the [<input type="date">] field. The regular expression checks the format ([fullmatch]: the entire string must match), while [strptime] checks for the existence of the date. An invalid date results in [None]: the action determines the outcome;
  • lines 50–51: the format [02d] outputs a two-digit integer, padded with zeros: [8:05];
  • lines 61–62: a date written out in full, in the language of the query, with [Babel] (example 16). The format is explicitly specified here: [EEEE], the day of the week spelled out; [d], the day; [MMMM], the month spelled out; [y], the year;
  • lines 69–73: reading an identifier sent by the browser (a parameter of URL, a hidden field). [\d{1,9}]: one to nine digits, which excludes characters, spaces, and numbers too large for a [INT] column. Anything coming from the browser may have been modified: it must be verified before use;
  • lines 82–85: the logged-in user; its absence (which should not occur in a protected action) is treated as an expired session;
  • lines 98–102: the patient (the entity [Client]) corresponding to the logged-in user. The token contains only the account ID: the patient is identified by the [clients.user] column. If it does not exist, it means the account has been deleted since the user logged in.

11.15.1. forms/regles.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# forms/regles.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The data entry rules common to "person" forms and FILTRES
# and WTForms (see Example 19): functions that transform the value
# received after validation.
# =========================================================================
TITRES = ("Mr", "Mme", "Melle")

# login: lowercase letters, numbers, period, hyphen, underscore—30 characters maximum
FORMAT_LOGIN = r"^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$"

# minimum password length CHOISI for a patient
MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN = 6


# "   dupont " -> "dupont"; "    " -> None
def nettoyer(valeur):
    if not isinstance(valeur, str):
        return valeur
    return valeur.strip() or None


# "   Dupont " -> "dupont": a username is always in lowercase
def login(valeur):
    valeur = nettoyer(valeur)
    return valeur.lower() if isinstance(valeur, str) else valeur


# an empty field -> None; for a password, spaces are not removed PAS
# spaces (they may be part of the password)
def vide_en_none(valeur):
    return valeur if valeur else None


# the hidden field [version]: an integer, or None if it is missing or empty.
# Text that is not a number: a ValueError, which WTForms converts
# into a field error, with this message (a translation key)
def version(valeur):
    if valeur in (None, ""):
        return None
    try:
        return int(valeur)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        raise ValueError("ERRORS.INVALID_FORM")

Input rules common to all forms, and the [WTForms] filters (example 19):

  • lines 8–14: allowed titles, the format of a username (lowercase letters, numbers, period, hyphen, underscore, up to 30 characters), and the minimum length of a password chosen by a patient;
  • Lines 18–21: The spaces surrounding an entry are removed; an empty entry becomes [None]. [a or b] is equivalent to [b] if [a] is “false” (in this case, an empty string);
  • lines 25–27: a username is always in lowercase;
  • lines 32–33: for a password, spaces are not removed, as they may be part of the password;
  • lines 39–45: the hidden version field (the optimistic lock): an integer, or [None]. A filter that returns a value like [ValueError] triggers a field error, with the error message matching that of the exception: a browser that submits anything other than a number would receive the “invalid form” error.

docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# forms/formulaires.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The fields in the "person" forms and their constraints (see examples
# 19 and 28). Three forms share the same identity fields
# (title, first name, last name):
#
#    ChampsPersonn               e title, first name, last name
#     ├─ FormulairePerson       ne + login / password FACULTATIFS, version
#                                   │ (ADMIN adds or modifies a doctor/client)
#     ├─ FormulaireInscripti    on + login / password / confirmation OBLIGATOIRES
#                                   │ (a patient creates an account)
#     └─ FormulaireMonComp      te + username, optional new password,
#                                    ACTUEL password required, version
#                                    (a patient modifies their account)
#
# A class WTForms that inherits from another class also inherits its fields.
#
# LIAISON: FormulairePersonne() reads the fields with the same name from the
# current POST query (request.form), and applies its filters to them
# (unnecessary spaces removed, login in lowercase...).
# VALIDATION: form.validate() then checks the constraints of each
# field, in order; the first one that fails stores its message in
# form.<field>.errors. These messages are translation strings (see i18n/*.json).
#
# Forms are used here solely to read and validate user input: the views
# generate their own <input> tags based on the view templates
# (see models/modeles_vues.py).
# =========================================================================
from flask_wtf import FlaskForm
from wtforms import PasswordField, StringField
from wtforms.validators import AnyOf, DataRequired, InputRequired, Length, Optional, Regexp

from rdvmedecins.forms import regles


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ common base
class ChampsPersonne(FlaskForm):

    titre = StringField(validators=[AnyOf(regles.TITRES, message="ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE")])

     # maximum lengths = those of the columns in SQL (VARCHAR(20)).
     # DataRequired stops field validation if the field is empty: the message
     # from Length is therefore never added to this one
    prenom = StringField(filters=[regles.nettoyer], validators=[
        DataRequired("ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_REQUIRED"),
        Length(max=20, message="ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_TOO_LONG")])

    nom = StringField(filters=[regles.nettoyer], validators=[
        DataRequired("ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED"),
        Length(max=20, message="ERRORS.LASTNAME_TOO_LONG")])


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ ADMIN
class FormulairePersonne(ChampsPersonne):

     # optional (see business/donnees.py): "Optional" stops validation of a
     # empty field, without an error
    login = StringField(filters=[regles.login], validators=[
        Optional(), Regexp(regles.FORMAT_LOGIN, message="ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN")])

     # optional; maximum 72 characters (if longer, bcrypt ignores the rest)
    password = PasswordField(filters=[regles.vide_en_none], validators=[
        Optional(strip_whitespace=False), Length(max=72, message="ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG")])

     # hidden field in the edit form (optimistic lock)
    version = StringField(filters=[regles.version])


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ patient registration
class FormulaireInscription(ChampsPersonne):

     # InputRequired: the entry must not be empty
    login = StringField(filters=[regles.login], validators=[
        InputRequired("ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED"),
        Regexp(regles.FORMAT_LOGIN, message="ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN")])

     # Two "Length" constraints, each with its own message
    password = PasswordField(filters=[regles.vide_en_none], validators=[
        InputRequired("ERRORS.PASSWORD_REQUIRED"),
        Length(min=regles.MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN, message="ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT"),
        Length(max=72, message="ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG")])

    confirmation = PasswordField(filters=[regles.vide_en_none], validators=[
        InputRequired("ERRORS.CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED")])


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ "Manage My Account"
class FormulaireMonCompte(ChampsPersonne):

    login = StringField(filters=[regles.login], validators=[
        InputRequired("ERRORS.LOGIN_REQUIRED"),
        Regexp(regles.FORMAT_LOGIN, message="ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN")])

     # optional: empty = password unchanged
    password = PasswordField(filters=[regles.vide_en_none], validators=[
        Optional(strip_whitespace=False),
        Length(min=regles.MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN, message="ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT"),
        Length(max=72, message="ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG")])

    confirmation = PasswordField(filters=[regles.vide_en_none])

     # the password ACTUEL, required for any account changes
    mot_de_passe_actuel = PasswordField(filters=[regles.vide_en_none], validators=[
        InputRequired("ERRORS.CURRENT_PASSWORD_REQUIRED")])

    version = StringField(filters=[regles.version])
  • Lines 38–51: the fields common to all three forms: title, first name, last name. The validator messages are translation keys: the view will translate them into the page’s language. The [AnyOf] validator accepts a value from a list. The maximum lengths are those of the SQL columns: a longer entry would be rejected by the database;
  • lines 55–67: the administrator form: a login and an optional password (the [Optional] validator stops validating an empty field without reporting an error; [strip_whitespace=False]: a password consisting of spaces is not considered empty), and the version;
  • lines 71–85: the patient registration form: username, password, and confirmation are required. Two validators, [Length], each with its own message: too short, too long;
  • lines 89–107: “Manage My Account”: an optional new password, and the current password, which is required for any changes.

A class named [WTForms], which inherits from another class, inherits its fields: the three forms share the fields of [ChampsPersonne]. The comparison of the password and its confirmation is not handled by the [EqualTo] validator (Example 19), but is performed by the action, which thus selects the message and the relevant field.

Note that these forms are used only to read and validate user input: the views do not call the [WTForms] fields to render them (Example 18); instead, they write their own [<input>] tags based on the view templates. This approach keeps the views identical across all three forms and gives the action complete control over what is displayed (never a password, for example). This is also the approach used in previous versions of the application.

# =========================================================================
# models/modeles_vues.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# "View models": what each action passes to its
# view, under the name [modele]. These are dataclasses: objects constructed
# once by the action, which the view simply reads
# ({{ modele.agenda.lignes }}...).
#
# Rule followed by all pages: no logic in the views. The
# actions prepare formatted data DÉJÀ ("Ms. Marie
# PELISSIER", "8:00 - 8:20", selectionne = True...) and already filtered according to
# the user’s role; the views simply place them in the HTML.
#
# Each page template has two fields, read by the template (templates/layout.html):
# titre_page, the page title key, and error, LE error message from
# the page, displayed at the bottom of the page (None: no error).
# =========================================================================
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from rdvmedecins.auth.captcha import Captcha
from rdvmedecins.forms import regles


# a message to be translated: its key and its parameters
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Message:
    cle: str
    parametres: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)


# an option from a drop-down list (doctor, patient)
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OptionVue:
    id: int
    libelle: str
    selectionne: bool


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ login
@dataclass
class LoginModele:
    titre_page: str
    erreur: Message | None
    login: str
    captcha: Captcha


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ calendar
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LigneAgendaVue:
    id_creneau: int
    horaire: str  # "8:00 - 8:20"
    libre: bool
    patient: str | None  # display name for a booked slot; None = “Reserved”
    moi: bool  # the logged-in patient’s appointment
    reservable: bool  # Display the "Book" button?
    url_reserver: str
    id_rv: int | None  # filled in only if the "Cancel" button is displayed


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AgendaVue:
    medecin: str
    jour: str
    lignes: list[LigneAgendaVue]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ReservationVue:
    id_creneau: int
    horaire: str
    clients: list[OptionVue]  # ADMIN / DOCTOR: patients to choose from
    patient: str | None  # USER: the patient is the patient themselves


@dataclass
class AgendaModele:
    titre_page: str
    erreur: Message | None
    medecins: list[OptionVue]
    id_medecin: int | None
    jour: str  # "yyyy-mm-dd"
    agenda: AgendaVue | None
    reservation: ReservationVue | None
    url_retour: str  # the displayed calendar, without a booking window
     # Patient who already has an upcoming appointment: the explanatory message
     # why there is no “Book” button
    info: str | None


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ "Person" forms

# the values displayed in the form fields (never the password)
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ValeursPersonne:
    titre: str = "Mr"
    prenom: str = ""
    nom: str = ""
    login: str = ""
    version: int | None = None


# the status of a rejected form: the message displayed SOUS for each field
# (field -> message key), and the fields to be highlighted in red (class
# Bootstrap is-invalid): those with a message, plus any others
# (duplicate first name + last name, username already taken...)
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EtatFormulaire:
    erreurs: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    champs_invalides: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)

    def erreur_de(self, champ: str) -> str | None:
        return self.erreurs.get(champ)

    def classe_invalide(self, champ: str) -> str:
        return "is-invalid" if champ in self.champs_invalides else ""


# an option from the list of titles
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OptionTitre:
    valeur: str
    selectionne: bool


# what the common fragment champs_personne.html uses (title, first name, last name):
# a base class from which the three form templates inherit
@dataclass
class FormulaireVue:
    titre_page: str
    erreur: Message | None
    valeurs: ValeursPersonne
    etat: EtatFormulaire

     # a property: reads like an attribute (modele.titres), but is calculated
    @property
    def titres(self) -> list[OptionTitre]:
        return [OptionTitre(t, t == self.valeurs.titre) for t in regles.TITRES]

    @property
    def mot_de_passe_min(self) -> int:
        return regles.MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN


@dataclass
class FormulairePersonneModele(FormulaireVue):
    creation: bool  # True: addition; False: modification
    action: str  # URL from POST
    url_liste: str


@dataclass
class InscriptionModele(FormulaireVue):
    pass


@dataclass
class MonCompteModele(FormulaireVue):
    pass


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ lists of doctors / clients

# translation keys specific to each person type
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ClesPersonnes:
    titre: str  # "Doctors"
    ajouter: str  # "Add a doctor"
    modifier: str  # "Edit a doctor"
    vide: str  # "No doctors."
    confirmer_suppression: str  # "Delete this doctor and their account?"
    ajoute: str  # "The doctor {name} has been added (login: {login})."
    modifie: str
    supprime: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PersonneVue:
    titre: str
    prenom: str
    nom: str
    login: str
    url_modifier: str
    url_supprimer: str


@dataclass
class ListePersonnesModele:
    titre_page: str
    erreur: Message | None
    cles: ClesPersonnes
    url_ajouter: str
    personnes: list[PersonneVue]


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ patient area
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RendezVousVue:
    id: int
    jour: str
    horaire: str
    medecin: str
    url_agenda: str


@dataclass
class EspaceModele:
    titre_page: str
    erreur: Message | None
    patient: str
    rendez_vous: list[RendezVousVue]


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ error page
@dataclass
class ErreurModele:
    titre_page: str
    erreur: Message | None
    code: int
    message: str

View models (*view models*): what each action passes to its view, under the name [modele]. The rule followed by all pages: no logic in the views. Actions prepare data that is already formatted (“Ms. Marie PELISSIER,” “8:00 – 8:20”) and already filtered according to the user’s role; views simply place this data into the HTML.

  • lines 26–28: a message to be translated: a key and its parameters. [field(default_factory=dict)]: the default value is a new, empty dictionary for each object. You cannot write [= {}]: this dictionary would be created only once and shared by all objects;
  • lines 33–36: an option from a drop-down list;
  • lines 41–45: the login page template. Each page template has two fields read by the template: [titre_page], the page title key, and [erreur], the error message displayed at the bottom of the page;
  • lines 50–58: a row in the calendar, already populated for the logged-in user: [patient] is equivalent to [None] for a time slot occupied by another patient, when the user is a patient (the view will display “Reserved”) ; [reservable] indicates whether to display the “Book” button; [id_rv] is populated only if the “Cancel” button is to be displayed. All these decisions are made by the action;
  • lines 69–73: the booking window: the list of patients for an administrator or doctor, the patient’s name for a patient;
  • lines 77–88: the calendar page template;
  • lines 108–116: the state of a rejected form, with two methods called by the views: the message for a field, and the class CSS that highlights it in red;
  • lines 129–142: the base class for the three form templates, used by the common fragment [champs_personne.html]. Its two properties calculate the list of titles (including the selected title) and the minimum length of a password;
  • Lines 146–158: The three form templates inherit from [FormulaireVue]. A [dataclass] that inherits from another adds its fields to those of its parent class;
  • lines 166–174: translation keys specific to doctors or clients: the same view displays both lists;
  • lines 198–211: the patient area;
  • lines 216–220: the error page.

The [controllers] folder contains one blueprint per part of the application (the login controller, [controllers/auth.py], was introduced with authentication):

BlueprintAddresses[langue][GET /langue/<code>][agenda][GET /agenda], [POST /agenda/reserver], [POST /agenda/annuler][medecins], [clients][/medecins/...], [/clients/...]: list, add, edit, delete[inscription][POST /inscription/acces], [GET], and [POST /inscription][espace][/mon-espace], [/mon-espace/annuler], [/mon-compte], [/mon-compte/supprimer]

All actions follow the same pattern: read and validate the request, call the business layer (via [ApplicationModel]), build the view model; or, for an action such as POST, post a flash message and redirect (flow PRG, example 20).

docs.title: 11.16.1. controllers/langue.py
docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# controllers/langue.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /language/fr, GET /language/en: the two buttons FR / EN on the
# navigation bar. Public road: You should be able to change the language before
# logging in.
#
# The selection is stored in a cookie: for each subsequent request, the
# function fixer_langue (see rdvmedecins/__init__.py) reads it and sets the
# language of the request (g.langue). You are then redirected back to the page you came from.
# =========================================================================
from datetime import timedelta
from urllib.parse import urlsplit

from flask import Blueprint, abort, current_app, redirect, request

from rdvmedecins.auth.securite import publique
from rdvmedecins.web.traducteur import COOKIE_LANGUE, LANGUES

langue = Blueprint("langue", __name__)


@langue.get("/langue/<code>")
@publique
def changer(code: str):
    if code not in LANGUES:
        abort(404)  # -> 404 error page (see web/erreurs.py)
    reponse = redirect(page_d_origine())
    reponse.set_cookie(COOKIE_LANGUE, code, max_age=timedelta(days=365), path="/",
                       httponly=True, samesite="Lax", secure=current_app.config["COOKIE_SECURE"])
    return reponse


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# the previous page, based on the "Referer" header HTTP sent by the
# browser. We only keep the path (/agenda?...): redirect to
# a complete address provided by the request would allow us to send
# the user to another site (a vulnerability known as an “open redirect”).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def page_d_origine() -> str:
    referer = request.headers.get("Referer")
    if not referer:
        return "/"
    url = urlsplit(referer)
    chemin = url.path
     # "//site.com/..." would be interpreted by the browser as an address
     # to a AUTRE site: also rejected
    if not url.scheme or not chemin.startswith("/") or chemin.startswith("//") \
            or chemin.startswith("/langue/"):
        return "/"
    return f"{chemin}?{url.query}" if url.query else chemin

The language selection from Example 22, with two additional precautions in [page_d_origine] (lines 40–51): a [Referer] without a schema ([http], [https]) is not a complete address, and a [Referer]—which would itself be a [/langue/...] address—would redirect to this action, creating a loop. In both cases, the user is redirected back to the site’s root. The cookie’s lifetime is specified by a [timedelta]: [set_cookie] accepts this just as well as a number of seconds.
