# =========================================================================
# controllers/agenda.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The calendar page: selecting a doctor and a day, that
# doctor’s schedule for that day, booking and canceling appointments.
#
#    GE T /agenda?idMedecin=1&day=2026-09-2             3 the page
#    GE T /agenda?idMedecin=1&day=2026-09-23&book=7     the same page, with
#                                                           the booking window
#                                                           for time slot 7 is open
#    POST /calendar/book                                   creates an appointment
#    POST /calendar/canc                                  el cancels an appointment
#
# The entire page is described by its URL: you can reload it, add it
# to your favorites, or use the browser’s “Back” button—without a single line
# of JavaScript.
#
# What everyone sees and can do:
#
#    | rol         e | displayed re           served slot           | Reserve | Cancel |
#   |---------------|-----------------------------------|--------------------|---------|
#    | ADMIN, DOCTOR | patient name                         | for     a patient | yes |
#                  |                                    |            | selected from list | |
#    | USER (patient)| “Reserved,” or SON name if it i s | for himself, if he| no (*) |
#                  | | his own            appointment          | does not already have an appointment| |
#                  |                                                         | | upcoming | |
#
#    (*) The patient cancels their appointment from their "My Account" page.
#
# CONFIDENTIALITÉ: for a patient, the names of the AUTRES patients are not
# simply hidden by the view—it is never included in the template
# passed to the view. The HTML sent to the browser therefore does not contain it,
# nor is it hidden (otherwise, simply “View Source” would reveal it).
#
# No reservations in the past: the “Reserve” button only appears
# for today and the following days (and the business layer would reject it
# in any case).
#
# Security: all URL /calendar operations require an authenticated user
# (see auth/securite.py: anything that isn’t @public). @roles_requis
# on an action also requires one of the listed roles. Without a valid token:
# return to /login; insufficient role: 403 page.
# =========================================================================
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date

from flask import Blueprint, abort, redirect, render_template, request, url_for

from rdvmedecins.auth.securite import roles_requis
from rdvmedecins.domain.agenda import AgendaMedecinJour
from rdvmedecins.entities import Client, Personne, Role
from rdvmedecins.metier import dates
from rdvmedecins.metier.exception import MetierException
from rdvmedecins.models.modeles_vues import (AgendaModele, AgendaVue, LigneAgendaVue, Message,
                                             OptionVue, ReservationVue)
from rdvmedecins.web import outils
from rdvmedecins.web.flash import flash_erreur, flash_succes
from rdvmedecins.web.services import application

agenda = Blueprint("agenda", __name__, url_prefix="/agenda")


# what the controller knows about the user, to determine what to display
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Droits:
    gestionnaire: bool  # ADMIN or DOCTOR
    patient: Client | None  # the logged-in client (role USER), otherwise None
    patient_peut_reserver: bool  # USER with no upcoming appointments


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /calendar
# The parameters for URL are read in raw format (request.args.get), to
# distinguish a ABSENT parameter (None) from a VIDE parameter (?idMedecin=).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@agenda.get("")
def afficher():
    erreur = None
    utilisateur = outils.utilisateur()
    droits = calculer_droits()

     # the day: the one from URL if it is valid, otherwise today
    jour = dates.aujourdhui()
    jour_brut = request.args.get("jour")
    if jour_brut is not None:
        jour_demande = outils.date_valide(jour_brut)
        if jour_demande is not None:
            jour = jour_demande
        else:
            erreur = "ERRORS.INVALID_DATE"
    jour_reservable = jour >= dates.aujourdhui()

     # the doctor: the one from URL; otherwise, for a logged-in doctor, the doctor themselves
    id_medecin_brut = request.args.get("idMedecin")
    id_medecin = outils.entier_positif(id_medecin_brut)
    if id_medecin_brut is None and utilisateur.role == Role.DOCTOR:
        medecin = application().get_medecin_by_user_id(utilisateur.user_id)
        id_medecin = medecin.id if medecin else None

     # the drop-down list of doctors
    medecins = [option(m, m.id == id_medecin) for m in application().get_all_medecins()]

     # the calendar, if a doctor is selected (and the date is valid)
    vue_agenda = None
    if id_medecin is not None and erreur is None:
        agenda_medecin = application().get_agenda_medecin_jour(id_medecin, jour)
        if agenda_medecin is None:
            erreur = "ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND"
        else:
            vue_agenda = agenda_vue(agenda_medecin, droits, jour_reservable)

     # the booking window: only if the requested time slot is
     # bookable by this user
    reservation = None
    id_creneau = outils.entier_positif(request.args.get("reserver"))
    if vue_agenda is not None and id_creneau is not None:
        ligne = next((l for l in vue_agenda.lignes if l.id_creneau == id_creneau and l.reservable),
                     None)
        if ligne is not None:
            reservation = ReservationVue(
                ligne.id_creneau,
                ligne.horaire,
                [option(c, False) for c in application().get_all_clients()]
                if droits.gestionnaire else [],
                outils.libelle(droits.patient) if droits.patient else None)

    modele = AgendaModele(
        titre_page="AGENDA.PAGE_TITLE",
        erreur=Message(erreur) if erreur else None,
        medecins=medecins,
        id_medecin=id_medecin,
        jour=outils.iso(jour),
        agenda=vue_agenda,
        reservation=reservation,
        url_retour=url_agenda(id_medecin, jour) if id_medecin is not None else url_for("agenda.afficher"),
        info=info_patient(droits, vue_agenda))
    return render_template("agenda.html", modele=modele)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /calendar/book   fields: idMedecin, day, idCreneau, idClient
#
# For a patient (USER), the field idClient is IGNORÉ: he books
# always books for himself. Trusting a field sent by the
# browser would allow a malicious patient to make a reservation in someone else’s name.
#
# "Post/Redirect/Get" pattern: regardless of the result, we do not
# generate a page here—we display a flash message and redirect
# to the calendar (see example 20).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@agenda.post("/reserver")
@roles_requis(Role.ADMIN, Role.DOCTOR, Role.USER)
def reserver():
    id_medecin, jour = lire_agenda_demande()
    id_creneau = outils.entier_positif(request.form.get("idCreneau"))
    if id_medecin is None or id_creneau is None:
        abort(400)  # -> “Invalid Request” page (see web/erreurs.py)
    utilisateur = outils.utilisateur()

    if utilisateur.est_patient:
        client = outils.patient_connecte(application())
    else:
        id_client = outils.entier_positif(request.form.get("idClient"))
        if id_client is None:
             # No patient selected: the booking window reopens
            flash_erreur("ERRORS.CHOOSE_PATIENT")
            return redirect(url_agenda(id_medecin, jour, id_creneau))
        client = application().get_client_by_id(id_client)

    creneau = application().get_creneau_by_id(id_creneau)
    if client is None:
        flash_erreur("ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND")
    elif creneau is None or creneau.id_medecin != id_medecin:
        flash_erreur("ERRORS.SLOT_NOT_FOUND")
    else:
        try:
             # the rules (not in the past, only one upcoming appointment per
             # patient, available time slot) are verified by the business logic layer
            application().ajouter_rv(jour, creneau, client)
            flash_succes("AGENDA.BOOKED")
        except MetierException as e:
             # same rule, but a message to the second person when it is the
             # patient themselves who is booking (“You already have...” rather
             # than “This patient...””). Other exceptions (true
             # errors) are not caught: 500 error.
            if e.cle == "ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT" and utilisateur.est_patient:
                flash_erreur("AGENDA.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO")
            else:
                flash_erreur(e.cle, **e.parametres)
    return redirect(url_agenda(id_medecin, jour))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /agenda/cancel    fields: idRv, idMedecin, day
# (a patient cancels SON an appointment from "My Account," not from here)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@agenda.post("/annuler")
@roles_requis(Role.ADMIN, Role.DOCTOR)
def annuler():
    id_medecin, jour = lire_agenda_demande()
    id_rv = outils.entier_positif(request.form.get("idRv"))
    if id_medecin is None or id_rv is None:
        abort(400)
    rv = application().get_rv_by_id(id_rv)
    if rv is None:
         # already canceled (by someone else, or by double-clicking)
        flash_erreur("ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND")
    else:
        application().supprimer_rv(rv)
        flash_succes("AGENDA.CANCELLED")
    return redirect(url_agenda(id_medecin, jour))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Who is logged in, and what actions are they authorized to perform on this page?
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def calculer_droits() -> Droits:
    if not outils.utilisateur().est_patient:
        return Droits(True, None, False)
    patient = outils.patient_connecte(application())
    rv_a_venir = application().get_rv_a_venir_client(patient.id)
    return Droits(False, patient, not rv_a_venir)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# The doctor’s schedule, formatted for viewing—and filtered according to permissions
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def agenda_vue(agenda_medecin: AgendaMedecinJour, droits: Droits, jour_reservable: bool) -> AgendaVue:
    id_medecin = agenda_medecin.medecin.id
    jour = agenda_medecin.jour
    lignes = []
    for cmj in agenda_medecin.creneaux_medecin_jour:
        creneau, rv = cmj.creneau, cmj.rv
        libre = rv is None
         # the logged-in patient’s appointment?
        moi = rv is not None and droits.patient is not None and rv.id_client == droits.patient.id
        lignes.append(LigneAgendaVue(
            id_creneau=creneau.id,
            horaire=outils.horaire(creneau),
            libre=libre,
             # LE privacy setting: a patient only sees the name
             # for the SON appointment; for others, None (the view displays “Reserved”)
            patient=outils.libelle(rv.client) if rv is not None and (droits.gestionnaire or moi) else None,
            moi=moi,
            reservable=libre and jour_reservable and (droits.gestionnaire or droits.patient_peut_reserver),
            url_reserver=url_agenda(id_medecin, jour, creneau.id),
            id_rv=rv.id if rv is not None and droits.gestionnaire else None))
    return AgendaVue(outils.libelle(agenda_medecin.medecin), outils.formater_jour(jour), lignes)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- Utility functions

# hidden fields idMedecin / day in the forms POST; (None, None) if they are invalid
def lire_agenda_demande() -> tuple[int | None, date | None]:
    id_medecin = outils.entier_positif(request.form.get("idMedecin"))
    jour = outils.date_valide(request.form.get("jour"))
    return (None, None) if id_medecin is None or jour is None else (id_medecin, jour)


# /calendar?idMedecin=1&day=2026-09-23[&reserver=7]: url_for appends to the end of
# the URL parameters that are not path variables
def url_agenda(id_medecin: int, jour: date, reserver: int | None = None) -> str:
    if reserver is None:
        return url_for("agenda.afficher", idMedecin=id_medecin, jour=outils.iso(jour))
    return url_for("agenda.afficher", idMedecin=id_medecin, jour=outils.iso(jour), reserver=reserver)


def option(p: Personne, selectionne: bool) -> OptionVue:
    return OptionVue(p.id, outils.libelle(p), selectionne)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# the informational message for a patient who already has an upcoming appointment
# (which is why there is no “Book” button), or None. Not needed if SON
# the appointment appears in the displayed calendar (in blue): this is the case
# after they’ve just scheduled it, in which case the message would be moved.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
def info_patient(droits: Droits, vue: AgendaVue | None) -> str | None:
    if droits.patient is None or droits.patient_peut_reserver:
        return None
    rv_affiche = vue is not None and any(ligne.moi for ligne in vue.lignes)
    return None if rv_affiche else "AGENDA.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO"

docs.title: 11.16.2.1. The URL for the page
docs.text: The entire page is described by its URL: [/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2026-09-26] displays Doctor #1’s schedule for that day; [&reserver=4] also opens the booking window for slot #4. The appointment booking window is therefore not opened by [JavaScript]: the server generates a page containing the window. This means you can reload the page, bookmark it, use the browser’s “Back” button, and the application works without [JavaScript] (the application’s only script is used for confirmation windows, and it works without it as well; see example 21).

docs.title: 11.16.2.2. GET /agenda
docs.text:
• lines 65–68: what the action knows about the user to determine the display: a “manager” (ADMIN or DOCTOR) or a patient, who may or may not make a reservation;
  • lines 83–91: the day: the day specified by URL if it is valid; otherwise, today. Parameters are read in raw format ([request.args.get]) to distinguish between a missing parameter ([None]: the default value is used, with no error) and an invalid parameter (an error is reported). Only today and the following days are bookable;
  • lines 94–98: the doctor: the one from URL; otherwise, for a logged-in doctor, the doctor themselves: a doctor can view their daily schedule directly upon logging in;
  • line 101: the drop-down list of doctors, read from the cache, with the selected doctor highlighted;
  • lines 104–110: the schedule, if a doctor is selected and the date is valid. A nonexistent doctor (an ID manually modified in URL) triggers an error message, not an error page;
  • lines 114–125: the booking window, only if the requested time slot exists and is bookable by this user: a patient who adds [&reserver=2] to URL for a time slot that is already booked will see nothing. [next(...)] searches for the corresponding calendar entry (example 21). The window displays a list of patients to an administrator; for each patient, it displays their own name;

docs.title: 11.16.2.3. POST /calendar/reserve
docs.text:
• line 152: All roles can make reservations. The decorator documents the rule and protects it in case a fourth role were to appear in the future;
  • lines 154–157: the form’s hidden fields. Invalid fields can only result from a manually crafted request: error 400;
  • lines 160–168: the patient for the appointment. For a patient, it is always the patient themselves: the field [idClient] is ignored. Trusting a field sent by the browser would allow a patient to book on behalf of another. For an administrator who has not selected a patient, the booking window reopens with a message;
  • lines 170–189: validations (the patient exists, the time slot exists and belongs to the doctor in the calendar), followed by the booking. Business rules are verified by the business logic layer; a [MetierException] becomes a flash error message. The message “only one upcoming appointment” is adapted when the patient makes the booking themselves (“You already have...” rather than “This patient already has...”);

docs.text:
• lines 217–222: user permissions. For a patient, it is necessary to view their upcoming appointments: an empty list is “incorrect,” hence [not rv_a_venir];
  • lines 228–248: the domain’s calendar, formatted for display and filtered according to permissions. This is where patient confidentiality comes into play (line 243): for a patient, the names of other patients are not merely hidden from view; they are never included in the template. The HTML sent to the browser therefore does not contain it, even if hidden (otherwise, a simple “View Source” would reveal it). The “Reserve” button appears only when there is an available time slot, a bookable day, and a user with the right to make a reservation; the “Cancel” button appears only for an administrator;

  • lines 262–265: the URL from the calendar. [url_for] adds the named parameters that are not path variables to URL as parameters (example 16);
  • lines 278–282: the informational message for a patient who already has an upcoming appointment: it explains why the “Book” buttons are missing. It is not displayed if the patient’s own appointment appears in the calendar (in blue), which is the case immediately after booking. [any(...)] returns [True] if either condition is true.

docs.title: 11.16.3. controllers/personnes.py
docs.text:
The management of doctors and clients, reserved for the administrator, is identical: same list, same form, same rules. Rather than writing the same actions twice, we write them once, in a blueprint factory.

# =========================================================================
# controllers/personnes.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The management of doctors and clients (reserved for ADMIN) are
# IDENTIQUES: same list, same form, same rules. Rather than
# writing the same actions twice, they are written once in a
# FABRIQUE DE BLUEPRINTS: the function creer_blueprint builds a
# complete blueprint from a "configuration" that specifies which QUOI to call and
# and QUELS labels to display. controllers/medecins.py and controllers/clients.py
# each calls the other using its own identifier. This results in the following for each:
#
#    GE T /doctor                  s list
#    GE T /doctors/add            empty form
#    POST /doctors/add            create
#    GE T /doctors/<id>/edit      pre-filled form
#    POST /doctors/<id>/edit      edit
#    POST /doctors/<id>/delete     deletion
#
# (and the corresponding URL under /clients). The views are also shared:
# templates/people/liste.html and templates/people/formulaire.html.
#
# SÉCURITÉ: a before_request DU BLUEPRINT requires the role ADMIN. It
# runs before the CHAQUE blueprint action—including those that are
# would add later: the rule is written once and for all.
# =========================================================================
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass

from flask import Blueprint, abort, redirect, render_template, url_for

from rdvmedecins.auth.securite import exiger_roles
from rdvmedecins.entities import Personne, Role
from rdvmedecins.forms.formulaires import FormulairePersonne
from rdvmedecins.metier.donnees import DonneesPersonne
from rdvmedecins.metier.exception import MetierException
from rdvmedecins.models.modeles_vues import (ClesPersonnes, EtatFormulaire, FormulairePersonneModele,
                                             ListePersonnesModele, Message, PersonneVue,
                                             ValeursPersonne)
from rdvmedecins.web import validation
from rdvmedecins.web.flash import flash_erreur, flash_succes


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# what each type of person must provide. The last five fields
# are FONCTIONS: medecins.py and clients.py store lambdas in them that
# call methods of the ApplicationModel (get_all_medecins...).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ConfigPersonnes:
    nom: str  # "doctors" or "clients": the name of the blueprint, and the beginning of the URL
    cles: ClesPersonnes
    lister: Callable[[], list[Personne]]  # () -> list
    trouver: Callable[[int], Personne | None]  # id -> person
    ajouter: Callable[[DonneesPersonne], Personne]  # data -> person created
    modifier: Callable[[int, DonneesPersonne], Personne]  # (id, data) -> person modified
    supprimer: Callable[[int], None]  # id -> nothing


def creer_blueprint(config: ConfigPersonnes) -> Blueprint:
    bp = Blueprint(config.nom, __name__, url_prefix=f"/{config.nom}")

     # the URL of an action from the CE blueprint: url("list") -> "/doctors"
    def url(action: str, **parametres) -> str:
        return url_for(f"{config.nom}.{action}", **parametres)

     # All actions in the blueprint are reserved for ADMIN
    @bp.before_request
    def reserve_admin():
        exiger_roles(Role.ADMIN)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     # GET /doctors (or /clients)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @bp.get("")
    def liste():
        personnes = [PersonneVue(p.titre, p.prenom, p.nom, login(p),
                                 url("formulaire_modification", id=p.id),
                                 url("supprimer", id=p.id))
                     for p in config.lister()]
        modele = ListePersonnesModele(config.cles.titre, None, config.cles, url("formulaire_ajout"),
                                      personnes)
        return render_template("personnes/liste.html", modele=modele)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     # GET /doctors/add
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @bp.get("/ajouter")
    def formulaire_ajout():
        return afficher_formulaire(None, ValeursPersonne(), {}, None, None)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     # POST /doctors/add
     # FormulairePersonne() reads the input; validate() checks it.
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @bp.post("/ajouter")
    def ajouter():
        form = FormulairePersonne()
        if not form.validate():
            return afficher_formulaire(None, valeurs_saisies(form), validation.erreurs_de(form),
                                       None, None)
        try:
            personne = config.ajouter(donnees(form))
        except MetierException as e:
            return afficher_erreur_metier(None, valeurs_saisies(form), e)
        flash_succes(config.cles.ajoute, **parametres(personne))
        return redirect(url("liste"))

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     # GET /doctors/<id>/edit
     # <int:id>: The ID must consist of numbers - /doctors/abc/edit does not
     # matches any URL (404 page)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @bp.get("/<int:id>/modifier")
    def formulaire_modification(id: int):
        personne = config.trouver(id)
        if personne is None:
            abort(404)
        valeurs = ValeursPersonne(personne.titre, personne.prenom, personne.nom, login(personne),
                                  personne.version)
        return afficher_formulaire(id, valeurs, {}, None, None)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     # POST /doctors/<id>/edit
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @bp.post("/<int:id>/modifier")
    def modifier(id: int):
        form = FormulairePersonne()
        if not form.validate():
            return afficher_formulaire(id, valeurs_saisies(form), validation.erreurs_de(form),
                                       None, None)
        try:
            personne = config.modifier(id, donnees(form))
        except MetierException as e:
            return afficher_erreur_metier(id, valeurs_saisies(form), e)
        flash_succes(config.cles.modifie, **parametres(personne))
        return redirect(url("liste"))

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
     # POST /doctors/<id>/delete
     # (A confirmation prompt asking "Are you sure?" appears before the
     # form; see static/js/app.js)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    @bp.post("/<int:id>/supprimer")
    def supprimer(id: int):
        personne = config.trouver(id)
        try:
            config.supprimer(id)
            flash_succes(config.cles.supprime, **parametres(personne))
        except MetierException as e:
            flash_erreur(e.cle, **e.parametres)
        return redirect(url("liste"))

     # ----------------------------------------------------------------- internal functions

     # id None: creation form; otherwise: update form.
     # errors: field -> message key; error: the key of the bottom
     # autres_champs: fields to be highlighted in red as well
    def afficher_formulaire(id: int | None, valeurs: ValeursPersonne, erreurs: dict[str, str],
                            erreur: str | None, autres_champs: list[str] | None):
        creation = id is None
        etat: EtatFormulaire = validation.etat(erreurs, autres_champs)
        modele = FormulairePersonneModele(
            titre_page=config.cles.ajouter if creation else config.cles.modifier,
            erreur=validation.message_page(erreurs, Message(erreur) if erreur else None),
            valeurs=valeurs,
            etat=etat,
            creation=creation,
            action=url("ajouter") if creation else url("modifier", id=id),
            url_liste=url("liste"))
        return render_template("personnes/formulaire.html", modele=modele)

     # a business rule rejected the write operation: the form is redisplayed,
     # with the user’s input and the business-layer message
    def afficher_erreur_metier(id: int | None, valeurs: ValeursPersonne, e: MetierException):
        if e.cle in ("ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND", "ERRORS.PATIENT_NOT_FOUND"):
             # which has since been deleted by another ADMIN: return to the list
            flash_erreur(e.cle)
            return redirect(url("liste"))
         # the message moves to the bottom of the page; the relevant fields, if any, are
         # highlighted in red so the user can immediately see what to correct
        return afficher_formulaire(id, valeurs, {}, e.cle, validation.CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER.get(e.cle))

    return bp


# what the user entered (excluding the password: it is never sent
# to the browser). form.<field>.data: the value, after filters
def valeurs_saisies(form: FormulairePersonne) -> ValeursPersonne:
    return ValeursPersonne(form.titre.data or "", form.prenom.data or "", form.nom.data or "",
                           form.login.data or "", form.version.data)


# the validated form -> the data expected by the business layer
def donnees(form: FormulairePersonne) -> DonneesPersonne:
    return DonneesPersonne(form.titre.data, form.nom.data, form.prenom.data, form.login.data,
                           form.password.data, form.version.data)


# {name} and {login} for the "added / modified / deleted" messages
def parametres(personne: Personne | None) -> dict[str, str]:
    if personne is None:
        return {"nom": "", "login": ""}
    return {"nom": f"{personne.prenom} {personne.nom}", "login": login(personne)}


def login(personne: Personne) -> str:
    return personne.user.login if personne.user else ""
  • lines 49–56: what each type of entity must provide: the blueprint name (which is also the beginning of URL), the translation keys, and five functions: list, find, add, edit, and delete. This is the same process as for business layer descriptors;
  • Lines 59–60: The factory creates a blueprint, whose name and the prefix of URL come from the configuration. The actions are internal functions of [creer_blueprint]: they have access to the factory’s variable [config]. Each call to [creer_blueprint] creates a new blueprint, with its own actions;
  • lines 63–64: the URL for an action in this blueprint: [url("liste")] returns [/medecins] for the doctors’ blueprint and [/clients] for the clients’ blueprint;
  • lines 67–69: a blueprint [before_request]: it runs before every action in the blueprint (and only in this one), after those of the application. All actions are thus reserved for the administrator, including any that might be added later: the rule is written once and applies to all;
  • lines 74–82: the list. [@bp.get("")]: the route is the prefix of the blueprint itself ([/medecins]);
  • lines 95–106: the add operation: form validation (input errors, displayed below the fields), call to the business layer (business errors, displayed at the bottom of the page), followed by a flash message and redirection to the list. The flash messages receive parameters: the person’s name and login;
  • lines 113–120: the edit form, pre-filled with the record’s version (optimistic locking). A nonexistent person results in a 404 page;
  • lines 125–136: the update, modeled after the add operation;
  • lines 143–151: the delete operation, confirmed beforehand by the confirmation window (example 21). A rejection by the business layer (a doctor who has appointments) results in a flash error message;
  • lines 158–170: the add form ([id] equals [None]) or edit form, along with its status (values, errors, fields highlighted in red);
  • lines 174–181: a business error: a person who has since been deleted by another administrator is returned to the list; the others redisplay the form, with the relevant fields highlighted in red;

  • lines 194–196: the validated form, converted into data for the business layer;

# =========================================================================
# controllers/medecins.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Physician management (ADMIN role only). All actions are
# generated by controllers/personnes.py: all that remains here is to call QUOI
# to call and QUELS to display labels.
#
# The configuration functions are LAMBDAS (functions without
# a name, written on the spot): application() is called only when
# the action is executed, during a request—the ApplicationModel does not exist
# when this module is imported.
# =========================================================================
from rdvmedecins.controllers.personnes import ConfigPersonnes, creer_blueprint
from rdvmedecins.models.modeles_vues import ClesPersonnes
from rdvmedecins.web.services import application

medecins = creer_blueprint(ConfigPersonnes(
    nom="medecins",
    cles=ClesPersonnes(
        titre="MEDECINS.TITLE",
        ajouter="MEDECINS.ADD",
        modifier="MEDECINS.EDIT",
        vide="MEDECINS.EMPTY",
        confirmer_suppression="MEDECINS.DELETE_CONFIRM",
        ajoute="MEDECINS.ADDED",
        modifie="MEDECINS.UPDATED",
        supprime="MEDECINS.DELETED"),
    lister=lambda: application().get_all_medecins(),
    trouver=lambda id: application().get_medecin_by_id(id),
    ajouter=lambda donnees: application().ajouter_medecin(donnees),
    modifier=lambda id, donnees: application().modifier_medecin(id, donnees),
    supprimer=lambda id: application().supprimer_medecin(id)))

The doctors’ blueprint, generated by [creer_blueprint] along with its configuration. The configuration functions are anonymous functions ([lambda]), which call [ApplicationModel]. Why not write [lister=application().get_all_medecins] directly? Because this module is executed when it is imported, at startup, before the application is created: [application()], which requires [current_app], would fail. The anonymous function defers the call until the action is executed, during a request.

docs.text:
# =========================================================================
# controllers/inscription.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# "Create a customer account": a patient who does not yet have an account
# creates one themselves. Routes PUBLIQUES (we don’t have an account yet, per
# definition):
#
#    POST /registration/log  in "Create a customer account" button on the
#                              authentication page: verifies the captcha from
#                              CETTE page, then opens the form
#    GE T /registrat        ion the form
#    POST /registrati        on the registration process, then returns to the login page
#
# The process is protected against bots by the UN CAPTCHA on the
# authentication page:
#    1. The "Create a Customer Account" button sends the login form
#       to /registration/access; if the CAPTCHA is entered correctly, the server
#       issues a token (see auth/passe_inscription.py);
#    2. Without a valid pass, /registration redirects to the
#       authentication page—typing URL directly does nothing;
#    3. The pass is used up upon creation: a solved CAPTCHA
#       allows you to create UN an account;
#    4. Additionally, the number of accounts created per hour per IP address is
#       limited (see auth/limiteur.py).
#
# The account created is exactly the one that ADMIN would create from the
# "Clients" page (same business-layer method: ajouter_client), if this
# is simply the patient CHOISIT entering their login and password (required,
# with confirmation).
# =========================================================================
from flask import Blueprint, current_app, redirect, render_template, request, url_for

from rdvmedecins.auth import passe_inscription
from rdvmedecins.auth.securite import publique
from rdvmedecins.controllers.auth import adresse_ip
from rdvmedecins.forms.formulaires import FormulaireInscription
from rdvmedecins.metier.donnees import DonneesPersonne
from rdvmedecins.metier.exception import MetierException
from rdvmedecins.models.modeles_vues import InscriptionModele, Message, ValeursPersonne
from rdvmedecins.web import validation
from rdvmedecins.web.flash import flash_erreur, flash_succes
from rdvmedecins.web.services import application, captchas, limiteur, passes

inscription = Blueprint("inscription", __name__, url_prefix="/inscription")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /registration/acces  s fields: captchaId, captcha (those on the
# authentication page; username and password, which are also sent, are ignored)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@inscription.post("/acces")
@publique
def acces():
    ip = adresse_ip()

     # too many accounts created recently from this address: no need to proceed further
    minutes = limiteur().minutes_blocage_inscription(ip)
    if minutes > 0:
        flash_erreur("ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS", minutes=str(minutes))
        return redirect(url_for("auth.afficher_login"))

     # captcha missing or incorrect: return to the authentication page, with
     # a new image (one failure counts as a failed login attempt)
    if not captchas().verifier(request.form.get("captchaId"), request.form.get("captcha")):
        limiteur().echec_login(ip, "")
        flash_erreur("ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT")
        return redirect(url_for("auth.afficher_login"))

     # Correct CAPTCHA: Grant access and open the form
    reponse = redirect(url_for("inscription.formulaire"))
    passe_inscription.deposer_cookie(reponse, passes().emettre(), current_app.config["COOKIE_SECURE"])
    return reponse


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@inscription.get("")
@publique
def formulaire():
    if not passes().est_valide(request.cookies.get(passe_inscription.COOKIE)):
        return retour_login()
    return afficher(ValeursPersonne(), {}, None, None)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@inscription.post("")
@publique
def creer():
    passe = request.cookies.get(passe_inscription.COOKIE)
    if not passes().est_valide(passe):
        return retour_login()
    ip = adresse_ip()
    form = FormulaireInscription()
    form.validate()
    valeurs = ValeursPersonne(form.titre.data or "Mr", form.prenom.data or "",
                              form.nom.data or "", form.login.data or "", None)

     # 1. Have too many accounts been created recently from this address?
    minutes = limiteur().minutes_blocage_inscription(ip)
    if minutes > 0:
        return afficher(valeurs, {}, Message("ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS", {"minutes": str(minutes)}),
                        None)

     # 2. All data entry errors at once (fields + confirmation):
         # the user corrects them all at once
    erreurs = validation.erreurs_de(form)
    if "password" not in erreurs and "confirmation" not in erreurs \
            and form.password.data != form.confirmation.data:
        erreurs["confirmation"] = "ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER"
    if erreurs:
        return afficher(valeurs, erreurs, None, None)

     # 3. Account creation (customer + account USER, in a single transaction)
    try:
        application().ajouter_client(DonneesPersonne(form.titre.data, form.nom.data,
                                                     form.prenom.data, form.login.data,
                                                     form.password.data))
    except MetierException as e:
         # Username or first name + last name already taken: the pass remains valid
        return afficher(valeurs, {}, Message(e.cle), validation.CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER.get(e.cle))

     # 4. The passcode has been used: it will not allow the creation of a second account
    passes().consommer(passe)
    limiteur().inscription_reussie(ip)

     # 5. Return to the login page; login credentials are pre-filled
    flash_succes("INSCRIPTION.DONE", login=form.login.data)
    reponse = redirect(url_for("auth.afficher_login", login=form.login.data))
    passe_inscription.effacer_cookie(reponse)
    return reponse


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- internal functions

# No valid token: return to the authentication page
def retour_login():
    flash_erreur("ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT")
    return redirect(url_for("auth.afficher_login"))


# the form; the password is never sent back to the browser
def afficher(valeurs: ValeursPersonne, erreurs: dict[str, str], erreur: Message | None,
             autres_champs: list[str] | None):
    modele = InscriptionModele("INSCRIPTION.TITLE", validation.message_page(erreurs, erreur),
                               valeurs, validation.etat(erreurs, autres_champs))
    return render_template("inscription.html", modele=modele)
  • Lines 51–72: The “Create a Customer Account” button on the login page submits the login form to this action (using the [formaction] attribute, Example 20). It checks the limit on account creations, then the CAPTCHA on the login page; if it is correct, it issues a token ([auth/passe_inscription.py]) and redirects to the registration form. A failure is counted as a failed login attempt (with an empty username);
  • lines 78–83: the form, only with a valid passcode: typing the address [/inscription] directly redirects to the login page;
  • lines 89–133: account creation: - the passcode, again; - [form.validate()] is called, but its result is ignored: we want all input errors at once, including any mismatch between the password and its confirmation, which is then verified by the action (provided both fields are otherwise valid). The user corrects them all at once; - the client and their account are created using the same business-logic method as for the administrator; - the pass is consumed, and the creation is counted by the limiter; - return to the login page, with a message and the login pre-filled (parameter [login] from URL). The pass cookie is cleared.

docs.title: 11.16.6. controllers/espace.py
docs.text:
The patient’s personal pages.

# =========================================================================
# controllers/espace.py
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The patient's pages (role USER), the one they see
# after logging in:
#
#    GE T /my-space               home page: [Gérer mon compte],
#                                   [Voir un agenda], and their upcoming appointment
#    POST /my-space/cancel        cancels the appointment SON
#    GE T /my-accou              nt account modification form
#    POST /my-accoun              t update
#    POST /my-account/delete      Delete account (and its appointments)
#
# Golden rule for this controller: the patient in question is TOUJOURS, the one from
# token (outils.patient_connecte), never an identifier sent by the
# browser. A patient can therefore neither view, modify, nor cancel what
# belongs to another patient, even by creating their own requests.
#
# Any modification or deletion of the account requires the password
# ACTUEL: someone who finds a session that has been left open would be unable to
# change the password or delete the account. Incorrect
# are counted as login failures (same limit).
# =========================================================================
from flask import Blueprint, redirect, render_template, request, url_for

from rdvmedecins.auth.auth_service import AuthService
from rdvmedecins.auth.securite import exiger_roles
from rdvmedecins.controllers.auth import adresse_ip
from rdvmedecins.entities import Client, Role
from rdvmedecins.forms.formulaires import FormulaireMonCompte
from rdvmedecins.metier.donnees import DonneesPersonne
from rdvmedecins.metier.exception import MetierException
from rdvmedecins.models.modeles_vues import (EspaceModele, Message, MonCompteModele, RendezVousVue,
                                             ValeursPersonne)
from rdvmedecins.web import outils, validation
from rdvmedecins.web.flash import flash_erreur, flash_succes
from rdvmedecins.web.services import application, auth_service, limiteur

espace = Blueprint("espace", __name__)


# All actions in this blueprint are reserved for the role USER
@espace.before_request
def reserve_patient():
    exiger_roles(Role.USER)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /my-space
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@espace.get("/mon-espace")
def espace_patient():
    patient = outils.patient_connecte(application())
    rendez_vous = [RendezVousVue(
        rv.id,
        outils.formater_jour(rv.jour),
        outils.horaire(rv.creneau),
        outils.libelle(rv.creneau.medecin),
         # link to the doctor’s schedule for that day: the patient sees their name there
        url_for("agenda.afficher", idMedecin=rv.creneau.id_medecin, jour=outils.iso(rv.jour)))
        for rv in application().get_rv_a_venir_client(patient.id)]
    modele = EspaceModele("ESPACE.TITLE", None, outils.libelle(patient), rendez_vous)
    return render_template("espace.html", modele=modele)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /my-space/cancel f  ield: idRv
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@espace.post("/mon-espace/annuler")
def annuler_rv():
    patient = outils.patient_connecte(application())
    id_rv = outils.entier_positif(request.form.get("idRv"))
    rv = application().get_rv_by_id(id_rv) if id_rv is not None else None
     # a nonexistent appointment, and one for a patient with the ID AUTRE, receive
     # the same response: we do not disclose information about other people’s appointments
    if rv is None or rv.id_client != patient.id:
        flash_erreur("ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND")
    else:
        application().supprimer_rv(rv)
        flash_succes("AGENDA.CANCELLED")
    return redirect(url_for("espace.espace_patient"))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /my-account
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@espace.get("/mon-compte")
def formulaire_compte():
    patient = outils.patient_connecte(application())
    valeurs = ValeursPersonne(patient.titre, patient.prenom, patient.nom, patient.user.login,
                              patient.version)
    return afficher(valeurs, {}, None, None)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /my-account
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@espace.post("/mon-compte")
def modifier_compte():
    patient = outils.patient_connecte(application())
    form = FormulaireMonCompte()
    form.validate()
    valeurs = ValeursPersonne(form.titre.data or patient.titre, form.prenom.data or "",
                              form.nom.data or "", form.login.data or "", form.version.data)

    erreurs = validation.erreurs_de(form)
    if "password" not in erreurs and form.password.data is not None \
            and form.password.data != form.confirmation.data:
        erreurs["confirmation"] = "ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER"
    if erreurs:
        return afficher(valeurs, erreurs, None, None)

     # the current password
    erreur_mot_de_passe = verifier_mot_de_passe_actuel(patient, form.mot_de_passe_actuel.data)
    if erreur_mot_de_passe is not None:
         # incorrect password: the message also goes to SOUS the field
        erreurs_champ = ({"mot_de_passe_actuel": erreur_mot_de_passe.cle}
                         if erreur_mot_de_passe.cle == "ERRORS.WRONG_CURRENT_PASSWORD" else {})
        return afficher(valeurs, erreurs_champ, erreur_mot_de_passe, None)

    try:
        client = application().modifier_client(patient.id, DonneesPersonne(
            form.titre.data, form.nom.data, form.prenom.data, form.login.data,
            form.password.data,  # None = unchanged
            form.version.data))
    except MetierException as e:
        return afficher(valeurs, {}, Message(e.cle), validation.CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER.get(e.cle))
     # the login and display name are DANS the token: one is issued
     # new; otherwise, the navigation bar would retain the old name
    flash_succes("MON_COMPTE.UPDATED")
    reponse = redirect(url_for("espace.espace_patient"))
    auth_service().deposer_jeton(reponse, client.user)
    return reponse


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /my-account/delete f  ield: mot_de_passe_suppression
# The account, the client, and TOUS their appointments are all deleted,
# and then the patient is logged out.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
@espace.post("/mon-compte/supprimer")
def supprimer_compte():
    patient = outils.patient_connecte(application())
    erreur_mot_de_passe = verifier_mot_de_passe_actuel(
        patient, request.form.get("mot_de_passe_suppression"))
    if erreur_mot_de_passe is not None:
        flash_erreur(erreur_mot_de_passe.cle, **erreur_mot_de_passe.parametres)
        return redirect(url_for("espace.formulaire_compte"))
    application().supprimer_client(patient.id)
    flash_succes("MON_COMPTE.DELETED")
    reponse = redirect(url_for("auth.afficher_login"))
    AuthService.effacer_jeton(reponse)
    return reponse


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- internal functions

# None if the current password is correct; otherwise, the error message
def verifier_mot_de_passe_actuel(patient: Client, mot_de_passe: str | None) -> Message | None:
    ip = adresse_ip()
    login = patient.user.login
    minutes = limiteur().minutes_blocage_login(ip, login)
    if minutes > 0:
        return Message("ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS", {"minutes": str(minutes)})
    ok = bool(mot_de_passe) and auth_service().valider_utilisateur(login, mot_de_passe) is not None
    if not ok:
        limiteur().echec_login(ip, login)
        return Message("ERRORS.WRONG_CURRENT_PASSWORD")
    return None


def afficher(valeurs: ValeursPersonne, erreurs: dict[str, str], erreur: Message | None,
             autres_champs: list[str] | None):
    modele = MonCompteModele("MON_COMPTE.TITLE", validation.message_page(erreurs, erreur), valeurs,
                             validation.etat(erreurs, autres_champs))
    return render_template("compte.html", modele=modele)
  • lines 43–45: All actions in the blueprint are reserved for the USER role;
  • lines 51–63: the patient’s dashboard: their upcoming appointments, formatted, each with a link to the doctor’s schedule for that day. The patient is always the one associated with the token ([outils.patient_connecte]), never an identifier sent by the browser: a patient cannot view, modify, or cancel another patient’s information;
  • lines 69–81: Canceling the patient’s appointment. A nonexistent appointment and another patient’s appointment receive the same response: no information about other patients’ appointments is disclosed (otherwise, a patient could discover which appointment numbers exist);
  • lines 87–92: the user’s account form, pre-filled;
  • lines 98–133: the edit: validation of fields and confirmation, verification of the current password, then a call to the business layer. The login and the displayed name are in the token: the action issues a new one; otherwise, the navigation bar would retain the old name until the next login;
  • lines 141–153: account deletion, which is also protected by the current password. The account, the client, and all their appointments are deleted together; the patient is logged out;
  • lines 159–169: The current password protects the account from anyone who might find a session that has been left open. Mistakes are counted as login failures, with the same limit: they cannot be used to guess the password.

docs.title: 11.17. The Views
docs.text: The [templates] folder contains the application’s [Jinja2] views: one template, seven fragments, and eight pages. All follow the same rule: no logic in the views. Actions pass them pre-prepared templates ([models/modeles_vues.py]); the views simply place the data into HTML and translate the text using the [t] function. They contain no hard-coded text: everything goes through the dictionaries.

docs.title: 11.17.1.1. templates/layout.html
docs.text:
<!doctype html>
{# =========================================================================
   templates/layout.html
   -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   Le gabarit COMMUN à toutes les pages (cf. exemple 15) : chaque page
   (agenda.html, login.html...) l'ÉTEND ({% extends %}) et remplit son bloc
   [contenu].

   Jinja2 ÉCHAPPE tout ce qu'il affiche avec {{ ... }} (les caractères
   < > & " ' deviennent < >...) : protection contre l'injection de HTML
   via un nom saisi, par exemple. Pour insérer du HTML tel quel, il faut le
   demander explicitement (filtre safe, cf. fragments/captcha.html).

   Messages : un succès s'affiche en HAUT de la page, une erreur en BAS, sur
   fond rose léger (fragment erreurs.html).

   Le gabarit partage les variables de la page : [modele] (le modèle de vue
   transmis par l'action, cf. models/modeles_vues.py), où il lit la clé du
   titre de la page ; [langue], [utilisateur], [chemin], [t], ajoutés à
   toutes les vues par web/modele_commun.py.
   ========================================================================= #}
<html lang="{{ langue }}">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  {# t(key): the translation of a key; here, the key is a VARIABLE (modele.titre_page) #}
  <title>{{ t(modele.titre_page) }} - {{ t("APP.TITLE") }}</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ url_for('static', filename='lib/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css') }}">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{{ url_for('static', filename='css/styles.css') }}">
</head>
<body>
  {# the flash messages posted by the previous request: read UNE times
     (get_flashed_messages les oublie aussitôt), puis répartis : les succès
     en haut, les erreurs en bas #}
  {% set flashes = get_flashed_messages(with_categories=true) %}
  <div class="container py-4">
    {% include "fragments/navbar.html" %}
    {% include "fragments/flash.html" %}
    <main>
      {% block contenu %}{% endblock %}
    </main>
    {% include "fragments/erreurs.html" %}
  </div>
  {# the "Are you sure?" window, hidden until needed #}
  {% include "fragments/confirmation.html" %}
  <script src="{{ url_for('static', filename='js/app.js') }}"></script>
</body>
</html>
  • line 22: the page language, provided by the context processor;
  • line 27: the page title. The title key is a variable ([modele.titre_page]): each page template provides one (the process from Example 22, using the view template instead of a [{% set %}] variable);
  • line 28: [Bootstrap] is part of the application, located in its [static] folder;
  • Line 35: Flash messages are read once by the template; [get_flashed_messages] immediately forgets them, and a second call would return an empty list. With [with_categories=true], the function returns tuples (category, message). The variable [flashes] is then read by the two fragments that display them: success messages at the top, error messages at the bottom. A variable defined by [{% set %}] is visible to the fragments included by [{% include %}];
  • lines 37–42: the navigation bar, success messages, page content, and error area;
  • lines 45–46: the confirmation window and the script that manages it (Example 21).

docs.title: 11.17.1.2. templates/fragments/navbar.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/navbar.html - la barre de navigation.

   Titre, FR/EN, rôle, nom, déconnexion - et un menu dont les entrées
   dépendent du rôle : "Médecins" et "Clients" n'apparaissent que pour
   l'ADMIN. Ce n'est qu'un confort d'affichage : la vraie protection, ce sont
