   obtient une page 403). Un patient (USER) a en plus son menu "Mon espace".

   Le menu de la page courante est mis en évidence (classe "active") :
   [chemin] est l'URL demandée (cf. web/modele_commun.py). Une macro écrit
   une fois le HTML d'une entrée du menu ; son paramètre [prefixe], facultatif
   (href par défaut), est le début des chemins pour lesquels l'entrée est active.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% macro entree(href, cle, prefixe=none) %}
<li class="nav-item">
  <a class="nav-link{{ ' active' if chemin.startswith(prefixe or href) }}" href="{{ href }}">{{ t(cle) }}</a>
</li>
{% endmacro %}
<nav class="navbar navbar-expand-sm navbar-dark bg-primary rounded mb-4 px-3">
  <span class="navbar-brand mb-0">{{ t("APP.TITLE") }}</span>

  {% if utilisateur %}
  <ul class="navbar-nav me-auto">
    {% if utilisateur.est_patient %}
    {# active for /my-space ET /my-account #}
    {{ entree("/mon-espace", "APP.MENU_MY_SPACE", "/mon-") }}
    {% endif %}
    {{ entree("/agenda", "APP.MENU_AGENDA") }}
    {% if utilisateur.est_admin %}
    {{ entree("/medecins", "APP.MENU_DOCTORS") }}
    {{ entree("/clients", "APP.MENU_PATIENTS") }}
    {% endif %}
  </ul>
  {% else %}
  <div class="me-auto"></div>
  {% endif %}

  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-2">
    {# FR / EN: simple links (GET /language/fr), with the active language highlighted #}
    <div class="btn-group btn-group-sm" role="group" aria-label="FR / EN">
      {% for code in ["fr", "en"] %}
      <a class="btn {{ 'btn-light' if langue == code else 'btn-outline-light' }}" href="/langue/{{ code }}">{{ code | upper }}</a>
      {% endfor %}
    </div>

    {% if utilisateur %}
    <span class="badge text-bg-light text-primary">{{ utilisateur.role }}</span>
    <span class="text-white">{{ utilisateur.nom }}</span>
    {# Logout is a POST: a form reduced to its button (and the anti-CSRF token) #}
    <form method="post" action="/logout" class="m-0">
      <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
      <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-light">{{ t("APP.LOGOUT") }}</button>
    </form>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
</nav>
  • lines 15–19: a menu item, highlighted (class [active]) if the path of the current page begins with its prefix. The parameter [prefixe] is optional ([none] to [Jinja2], just as [None] to [Python]); otherwise, it is the entry’s address ([prefixe or href]). The “My Space” entry is prefixed with [/mon-]: it is active for both [/mon-espace] and [/mon-compte];
  • lines 23–37: the menu depends on the role: “My Account” for a patient, “Doctors” and “Clients” for the administrator. This is merely a display convenience; the real security comes from role-based controls on actions. A patient who manually enters [/medecins] will receive a 403 error page;
  • lines 42–44: the buttons FR and EN are simply links to [/langue/fr] and [/langue/en];
  • lines 48–54: role, username, and logout: a POST form reduced to its button, with the anti-CSRF token.

docs.title: 11.17.1.3. templates/fragments/flash.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/flash.html - les messages de SUCCÈS déposés par
   l'action précédente (rendez-vous enregistré, médecin ajouté...),
   affichés une seule fois, en haut de la page (cf. web/flash.py).
   Un message flash d'ERREUR, lui, est affiché en bas de la page, par
   fragments/erreurs.html.

   [flashes] : la liste des couples (catégorie, message), lue par le gabarit.
   t(message.cle, message.parametres) : le message dont la clé est
   message.cle, avec en paramètre le dictionnaire des valeurs de {nom},
   {login}... (cf. web/traducteur.py).
   ========================================================================= #}
{% for categorie, message in flashes if categorie == "success" %}
<div class="alert alert-success" role="status">{{ t(message.cle, message.parametres) }}</div>
{% endfor %}
  • line 13: a [for] loop from [Jinja2] can filter its elements: [for ... in ... if condition] iterates only over elements that satisfy the condition. Each element is a pair, with both parts stored in two variables;
  • line 14: the message is a dictionary (see [web/flash.py]): its key and its parameters. The dot notation in [Jinja2] also reads the keys of a dictionary (example 13).

docs.title: 11.17.1.4. templates/fragments/erreurs.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/erreurs.html - la zone d'erreur, en BAS de chaque
   page, sur fond rose léger (classe .zone-erreur, cf. static/css/styles.css).

   Elle regroupe les deux sources d'erreur possibles :
     - modele.erreur : l'erreur de la page affichée (formulaire refusé, login
       ou prénom + nom déjà utilisés, date invalide, mot de passe incorrect...) ;
     - les messages flash d'erreur, déposés par l'action précédente avant une
       redirection (créneau déjà réservé, suppression refusée...).

   Une boucle for peut filtrer ses éléments : "for ... in ... if condition".
   role="alert" : un lecteur d'écran annonce le message dès l'affichage de
   la page, même s'il se trouve en bas.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% set erreurs_flash = flashes | selectattr(0, "equalto", "danger") | list %}
{% if modele.erreur or erreurs_flash %}
<div class="zone-erreur" role="alert">
  {% if modele.erreur %}
  <div>{{ t(modele.erreur.cle, modele.erreur.parametres) }}</div>
  {% endif %}
  {% for categorie, message in erreurs_flash %}
  <div>{{ t(message.cle, message.parametres) }}</div>
  {% endfor %}
</div>
{% endif %}
  • line 15: error flash messages, extracted by two filters: [selectattr(0, "equalto", "danger")] keeps only those elements whose [0] attribute (the first element of the pair, the category) is equal to ["danger"]; [list] converts the result into a list (filters of this type return an iterator that can only be traversed once and cannot be checked to see if it is empty);
  • Lines 16–25: The error area combines the two sources of errors: errors from the displayed page (a rejected form, an invalid date) and errors generated by the previous action before a redirect (a time slot already taken, a deletion rejected). The area exists only if there is at least one error.

docs.title: 11.17.1.5. templates/fragments/confirmation.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/confirmation.html - la fenêtre modale "Êtes-vous sûr ?".

   Elle remplace la boîte window.confirm() du navigateur, qu'on ne peut ni
   mettre en forme, ni traduire (ses boutons restent dans la langue du
   navigateur, pas dans celle de la page).

   Une SEULE fenêtre pour toute la page, cachée (d-none) au départ. Ses
   libellés sont traduits ici, par le serveur, comme le reste de la page ;
   le petit script static/js/app.js se contente de l'afficher, d'y placer
   le message propre au formulaire (attribut data-confirmation), et d'envoyer
   le formulaire si l'utilisateur confirme.

   Mêmes classes Bootstrap que la fenêtre de réservation (fragments/reservation.html).
   ========================================================================= #}
<div id="modale-confirmation" class="d-none">
  <div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
  <div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true"
       aria-labelledby="modale-confirmation-titre" aria-describedby="modale-confirmation-message">
    <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
      <div class="modal-content">
        <div class="modal-header">
          <h5 class="modal-title" id="modale-confirmation-titre">{{ t("CONFIRMATION.TITLE") }}</h5>
          <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-action="non" aria-label="{{ t('BOOKING_DIALOG.CLOSE_ARIA') }}"></button>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-body">
          <p class="mb-0" id="modale-confirmation-message"></p>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-footer">
          {# "No, go back" rather than "Cancel": the question is sometimes
             « Annuler ce rendez-vous ? », et un bouton "Annuler" y serait ambigu #}
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" data-action="non">{{ t("CONFIRMATION.NO") }}</button>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-danger" data-action="oui">{{ t("CONFIRMATION.YES") }}</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

The confirmation window from Example 21, with labels translated by the server (the browser’s [window.confirm()] box displays its buttons in the browser’s language, not the page’s language), a close button, and accessibility attributes: [aria-labelledby] and [aria-describedby] refer to the window’s title and message, which screen readers announce when the window opens. The “No, go back” button is preferred over “Cancel”: the question is sometimes “Cancel this appointment?”, and a “Cancel” button would be ambiguous in that context.

docs.title: 11.17.1.6. templates/fragments/captcha.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/captcha.html - le captcha de la page d'authentification
   (cf. auth/captcha.py). Il protège à la fois la connexion et l'accès à la
   création de compte (bouton "Créer un compte client").
   Une macro, dont le paramètre est un objet Captcha (id, svg).

   Le filtre safe : l'image SVG est insérée TELLE QUELLE dans la page, sans
   échappement. C'est sans danger ici parce que ce SVG est fabriqué par le
   serveur lui-même et ne contient rien qui vienne de l'utilisateur - on ne
   ferait JAMAIS cela avec une saisie.

   Le champ caché captchaId dit au serveur QUEL captcha vérifier ; la bonne
   réponse, elle, n'est jamais envoyée au navigateur.
   "Autre image" recharge simplement la page ([chemin] = l'URL courante).
   Une macro ne voit pas les variables de la page qui l'appelle ("with
   context" : si, lors de l'importation, cf. login.html) : ici, t et chemin.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% macro captcha(captcha) %}
<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="captcha">{{ t("CAPTCHA.LABEL") }}</label>
  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-3 mb-2">
    <div class="captcha-image" role="img" aria-label="{{ t('CAPTCHA.IMAGE_ALT') }}">{{ captcha.svg | safe }}</div>
    <a class="small" href="{{ chemin }}">{{ t("CAPTCHA.NEW_IMAGE") }}</a>
  </div>
  <input type="hidden" name="captchaId" value="{{ captcha.id }}">
  <input id="captcha" name="captcha" type="text" maxlength="10" autocomplete="off" autocapitalize="off"
         spellcheck="false" required class="form-control">
  <div class="form-text">{{ t("CAPTCHA.HELP") }}</div>
</div>
{% endmacro %}
  • line 18: a macro that receives an object [Captcha];
  • line 22: the image SVG, inserted as-is (example 27). The attribute [role="img"] and its [aria-label] describe the image to screen readers;
  • line 23: the “Other image” link simply reloads the page: each view generates a new CAPTCHA;
  • Lines 25–27: the CAPTCHA ID and the input field. [autocapitalize="off"] and [spellcheck="false"] prevent phones from modifying the input (initial uppercase letter, spell check).

By default, an imported macro cannot access the variables of the page that imports it: the function [t] and the variable [chemin], provided by the context processor, would be unknown to it. This is why [login.html] imports it with the reference [with context].

docs.title: 11.17.1.7. templates/fragments/champs_personne.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/champs_personne.html - les champs d'identité (titre,
   prénom, nom), communs à trois formulaires : médecin/client de l'ADMIN,
   "Créer un compte client" et "Gérer mon compte".
   Le fragment, inséré par {% include %}, lit la variable [modele] de la
   page qui l'insère (un FormulaireVue, cf. models/modeles_vues.py) :
   valeurs, message sous chaque champ, champs encadrés en rouge.

   selected : un attribut booléen, écrit si l'option est choisie, omis sinon.
   etat.classe_invalide(champ) : "is-invalid" (encadré rouge de Bootstrap)
   pour un champ refusé, "" sinon.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% set etat = modele.etat %}
<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="titre">{{ t("PERSONNES.TITLE_LABEL") }}</label>
  <select id="titre" name="titre" class="form-select {{ etat.classe_invalide('titre') }}">
    {% for titre in modele.titres %}
    <option value="{{ titre.valeur }}"{{ " selected" if titre.selectionne }}>{{ titre.valeur }}</option>
    {% endfor %}
  </select>
  {% if etat.erreur_de("titre") %}
  <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(etat.erreur_de("titre")) }}</div>
  {% endif %}
</div>

<div class="row g-3 mb-3">
  <div class="col-sm-6">
    <label class="form-label" for="prenom">{{ t("PERSONNES.FIRSTNAME_LABEL") }}</label>
    <input id="prenom" name="prenom" type="text" maxlength="20" required
           class="form-control {{ etat.classe_invalide('prenom') }}" value="{{ modele.valeurs.prenom }}">
    {% if etat.erreur_de("prenom") %}
    <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(etat.erreur_de("prenom")) }}</div>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
  <div class="col-sm-6">
    <label class="form-label" for="nom">{{ t("PERSONNES.LASTNAME_LABEL") }}</label>
    <input id="nom" name="nom" type="text" maxlength="20" required
           class="form-control {{ etat.classe_invalide('nom') }}" value="{{ modele.valeurs.nom }}">
    {% if etat.erreur_de("nom") %}
    <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(etat.erreur_de("nom")) }}</div>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
</div>

The identity fields (title, first name, last name), which are common to all three forms in the application. The fragment, inserted by [{% include %}], reads the variable [modele] from the page that inserts it: a template that inherits from [FormulaireVue].

  • Lines 16–20: the list of titles, calculated by the template’s [titres] property, with the selected title highlighted;
  • lines 29–30: the first name input field, with the value to be redisplayed, and the class [is-invalid] if the field is rejected ([etat.classe_invalide('prenom')]);
  • lines 31–33: the message below the field, translated.

The attributes [maxlength] and [required] are browser controls. The application’s forms include the attribute [novalidate] (Example 19): these checks are not performed before submission; validation is handled by the server. [maxlength], on the other hand, always prevents users from entering more characters than a column can accommodate.

docs.title: 11.17.1.8. templates/fragments/reservation.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/fragments/reservation.html - la fenêtre de réservation de
   l'agenda.

   Les VRAIES classes Bootstrap d'une fenêtre modale (.modal,
   .modal-backdrop...), rendues visibles "en dur" (show d-block) plutôt que
   par le JavaScript de Bootstrap. C'est le SERVEUR qui décide de l'afficher
   (paramètre &reserver=... de l'URL), et la fermer revient à suivre un lien
   vers la même page sans ce paramètre.

   Le fragment lit directement la variable [modele] de la page qui l'insère
   (un AgendaModele).
   ========================================================================= #}
{% set reservation = modele.reservation %}
<div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
<div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="titre-reservation">
  <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
    <form method="post" action="/agenda/reserver" class="modal-content">
      <div class="modal-header">
        <h5 class="modal-title" id="titre-reservation">{{ t("BOOKING_DIALOG.TITLE") }}</h5>
        <a class="btn-close" href="{{ modele.url_retour }}" aria-label="{{ t('BOOKING_DIALOG.CLOSE_ARIA') }}"></a>
      </div>

      <div class="modal-body">
        <p>{{ t("BOOKING_DIALOG.SLOT", horaire=reservation.horaire) }}</p>

        {# what else the server needs to know besides the selected patient #}
        <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="idMedecin" value="{{ modele.id_medecin }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="jour" value="{{ modele.jour }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="idCreneau" value="{{ reservation.id_creneau }}">

        {# A patient makes a reservation for themselves: no list to choose from
           (et le serveur ignore de toute façon un éventuel idClient) #}
        {% if reservation.patient %}
        <p class="mb-0">
          <span>{{ t("BOOKING_DIALOG.PATIENT_LABEL") }}</span> :
          <strong>{{ reservation.patient }}</strong>
        </p>
        {% else %}
        <label class="form-label" for="idClient">{{ t("BOOKING_DIALOG.PATIENT_LABEL") }}</label>
        <select id="idClient" name="idClient" class="form-select" required autofocus>
          <option value="">{{ t("BOOKING_DIALOG.CHOOSE_PATIENT") }}</option>
          {% for client in reservation.clients %}
          <option value="{{ client.id }}">{{ client.libelle }}</option>
          {% endfor %}
        </select>
        {% endif %}
      </div>

      <div class="modal-footer">
        <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{{ modele.url_retour }}">{{ t("BOOKING_DIALOG.CANCEL") }}</a>
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{{ t("BOOKING_DIALOG.CONFIRM") }}</button>
      </div>
    </form>
  </div>
</div>

The reservation window. It uses the actual classes of a modal window from [Bootstrap] ([modal], [modal-backdrop]...), made visible "hard-coded" ([show d-block]) rather than via the [JavaScript] of [Bootstrap]: the server decides whether to display it (the [reserver] parameter of URL), and closing it is equivalent to following a link to the same page without that parameter ([modele.url_retour]).

  • Lines 29–31: Hidden fields: information the server needs to know, in addition to the selected patient;
  • lines 35–48: a patient makes a reservation for themselves: their name is displayed, with no list to choose from (and the server would ignore a [idClient] field anyway). For an administrator, the list of patients—whose first option, with an empty value, prompts a selection—is displayed.

docs.title: 11.17.2.1. templates/login.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/login.html - le formulaire de connexion (cf. controllers/auth.py).
   Un <form> HTML ordinaire : le navigateur envoie lui-même login, mot de
   passe et réponse au captcha en POST /login, sans JavaScript. En cas
   d'échec, le serveur renvoie CETTE page, avec le login déjà saisi, un
   NOUVEAU captcha et l'erreur, affichée en bas de page par le gabarit.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends "layout.html" %}
{# with context: the macro sees the variables on this page (t, path) #}
{% from "fragments/captcha.html" import captcha with context %}

{% block contenu %}
{% set login_saisi = modele.login != "" %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-sm-8 col-md-6 col-lg-5">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{{ t("LOGIN.TITLE") }}</h5>

      <form method="post" action="/login">
        <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">{{ t("LOGIN.LOGIN_LABEL") }}</label>
          {# autofocus: a Boolean attribute, set if the condition is true, omitted otherwise #}
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" class="form-control" autocomplete="username"
                 value="{{ modele.login }}" required{{ " autofocus" if not login_saisi }}>
        </div>
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="password">{{ t("LOGIN.PASSWORD_LABEL") }}</label>
          <input id="password" name="password" type="password" class="form-control"
                 autocomplete="current-password" required{{ " autofocus" if login_saisi }}>
        </div>

        {{ captcha(modele.captcha) }}

        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary w-100">{{ t("LOGIN.SUBMIT") }}</button>

        {# No account yet: a patient can create one themselves.
           Ce n'est PAS un simple lien : c'est un second bouton d'envoi de
           CE formulaire, qui part vers une autre adresse (formaction). Le
           serveur y vérifie le captcha ci-dessus avant d'ouvrir la page de
           création de compte (cf. controllers/inscription.py).
           formnovalidate : le navigateur n'exige pas login et mot de passe
           (inutiles pour créer un compte) ; c'est le serveur qui vérifie
           le captcha. Entrée dans un champ déclenche toujours le PREMIER
           bouton du formulaire, "Se connecter". #}
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-outline-primary w-100 mt-3"
                formaction="/inscription/acces" formnovalidate>{{ t("LOGIN.CREATE_ACCOUNT") }}</button>
        <div class="form-text text-center">{{ t("LOGIN.CREATE_ACCOUNT_HELP") }}</div>
      </form>

      <div class="text-muted small mt-3">
        <span>{{ t("LOGIN.DEMO_ACCOUNTS") }}</span>
        <ul class="mb-0 mt-1">
          <li><code>admin</code> - <span>{{ t("LOGIN.DEMO_ADMIN") }}</span></li>
          <li><code>pelissier</code>, <code>tatou</code>, <code>dupont</code> - <span>{{ t("LOGIN.DEMO_DOCTOR") }}</span></li>
          <li><code>martin</code>, <code>durand</code>, <code>bistrou</code>, <code>german</code> - <span>{{ t("LOGIN.DEMO_USER") }}</span></li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}
  • line 10: the macro is imported, along with the page context;
  • line 13: the cursor is placed in the login field if it is empty, or in the password field otherwise (after a failed login attempt or after creating an account): the Boolean attribute [autofocus] is set to one or the other;
  • lines 24–30: the values of the [autocomplete] attribute help browser password managers fill out the form;
  • lines 46–47: The “Create a Customer Account” button is not a link, but a second button to submit this form, which sends it to a different address ([formaction], example 20). The server verifies the CAPTCHA there before opening the account creation page. [formnovalidate]: The browser does not require the username and password, marked as [required], which are unnecessary for creating an account. Pressing the Enter key in a field always triggers the first button on the form, “Log In.”

docs.title: 11.17.2.2. templates/agenda.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/agenda.html - la page principale (cf. controllers/agenda.py).
   Trois blocs :
     1. le choix du médecin et du jour ;
     2. l'agenda ;
     3. la fenêtre de réservation (fragments/reservation.html).
   Une éventuelle erreur (date invalide, médecin inconnu) est affichée en
   bas de la page par le gabarit (cf. fragments/erreurs.html).
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends "layout.html" %}

{% block contenu %}
  {# 1. Selecting a doctor and date: a GET form, which reloads
        simplement cette page avec ?idMedecin=...&jour=... dans l'URL #}
  <form method="get" action="/agenda" class="card p-3 mb-3">
    <div class="row g-2 align-items-end">
      <div class="col-sm-5">
        <label class="form-label" for="idMedecin">{{ t("DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.DOCTOR_LABEL") }}</label>
        <select id="idMedecin" name="idMedecin" class="form-select" required>
          <option value="">{{ t("DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.CHOOSE_DOCTOR") }}</option>
          {% for medecin in modele.medecins %}
          <option value="{{ medecin.id }}"{{ " selected" if medecin.selectionne }}>{{ medecin.libelle }}</option>
          {% endfor %}
        </select>
      </div>
      <div class="col-sm-4">
        <label class="form-label" for="jour">{{ t("DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.DAY_LABEL") }}</label>
        <input id="jour" name="jour" type="date" class="form-control" value="{{ modele.jour }}" required>
      </div>
      <div class="col-sm-3">
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary w-100">{{ t("DOCTOR_DAY_PICKER.VIEW_AGENDA") }}</button>
      </div>
    </div>
  </form>

  {# Patient who already has an upcoming appointment: why there is no "Book" button #}
  {% if modele.info %}
  <div class="alert alert-info">
    <span>{{ t(modele.info) }}</span>
    <a href="/mon-espace" class="alert-link">{{ t("APP.MENU_MY_SPACE") }}</a>
  </div>
  {% endif %}

  {# 2. The calendar #}
  {% set agenda = modele.agenda %}
  {% if agenda %}
  <div class="card p-3">
    <h5>{{ t("AGENDA.TITLE_PREFIX") }} {{ agenda.jour }} - {{ agenda.medecin }}</h5>

    {% if agenda.lignes %}
    <table class="table table-hover align-middle">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>{{ t("AGENDA.COLUMN_SLOT") }}</th>
          <th>{{ t("AGENDA.COLUMN_STATUS") }}</th>
          <th></th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {% for ligne in agenda.lignes %}
        <tr class="{{ 'creneau-libre' if ligne.reservable }}">
          <td>{{ ligne.horaire }}</td>
          <td>
            {# [patient] is populated only if the user has permission to
               voir ce nom (ADMIN, DOCTOR, ou le patient pour SON
               rendez-vous) - sinon, simplement « Réservé » #}
            {% if ligne.libre %}
            <span class="badge text-bg-success">{{ t("AGENDA.FREE") }}</span>
            {% elif ligne.patient %}
            <span class="badge {{ 'text-bg-primary' if ligne.moi else 'text-bg-secondary' }}">{{ ligne.patient }}</span>
            {% else %}
            <span class="badge text-bg-secondary">{{ t("AGENDA.BOOKED_BY_OTHER") }}</span>
            {% endif %}
          </td>
          <td>
            {# The displayed buttons were determined by the controller
               (reservable, id_rv) selon le rôle de l'utilisateur.
               "Réserver" est un simple lien : il rouvre cette page
               avec la fenêtre de réservation de ce créneau #}
            {% if ligne.reservable %}
            <a class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-success" href="{{ ligne.url_reserver }}">{{ t("AGENDA.BOOK") }}</a>
            {% endif %}
            {# "Cancel" MODIFIE data: this is therefore a POST #}
            {% if ligne.id_rv %}
            <form method="post" action="/agenda/annuler" class="m-0"
                  data-confirmation="{{ t('AGENDA.CANCEL_CONFIRM') }}">
              <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
              <input type="hidden" name="idRv" value="{{ ligne.id_rv }}">
              <input type="hidden" name="idMedecin" value="{{ modele.id_medecin }}">
              <input type="hidden" name="jour" value="{{ modele.jour }}">
              <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger">{{ t("AGENDA.CANCEL_APPOINTMENT") }}</button>
            </form>
            {% endif %}
          </td>
        </tr>
        {% endfor %}
      </tbody>
    </table>
    {% else %}
    <p class="text-muted mb-0">{{ t("AGENDA.NO_SLOTS") }}</p>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
  {% else %}
  <p class="text-muted">{{ t("AGENDA.EMPTY_STATE") }}</p>
  {% endif %}

  {# 3. The reservation window, only if the URL contains &reserve=... #}
  {% if modele.reservation %}
  {% include "fragments/reservation.html" %}
  {% endif %}
{% endblock %}
  • Lines 15–34: Selecting a doctor and a day: a form named GET (Example 17), which simply reloads the page with the parameters [idMedecin] and [jour] in URL. The [<input type="date">] field displays its values in the [aaaa-mm-jj] format, regardless of the language in which the browser displays it;
  • lines 37–42: the informational message for a patient who already has an upcoming appointment;
  • Lines 61–95: An entry in the schedule. There are three possible statuses: available, booked with the patient’s name (in blue if it’s the logged-in patient’s appointment), or booked without the name (“Reserved”). The buttons displayed are determined by the action. “Reserve” is a simple link: it reopens this page with the reservation window for that time slot. “Cancel” modifies data: it is a POST form, with its confirmation request (example 21);
  • lines 108–110: the booking window, only if the action has prepared it.

docs.title: 11.17.2.3. templates/people/liste.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/personnes/liste.html - la liste des médecins OU des clients (ADMIN).
   Une seule vue pour les deux : les libellés propres à chacun arrivent dans
   modele.cles (cf. controllers/medecins.py / controllers/clients.py).
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends "layout.html" %}

{% block contenu %}
  <div class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center mb-3">
    <h4 class="mb-0">{{ t(modele.cles.titre) }}</h4>
    <a class="btn btn-primary" href="{{ modele.url_ajouter }}">{{ t(modele.cles.ajouter) }}</a>
  </div>

  <div class="card p-3">
    {% if modele.personnes %}
    <table class="table table-hover align-middle mb-0">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>{{ t("PERSONNES.COLUMN_TITLE") }}</th>
          <th>{{ t("PERSONNES.COLUMN_FIRSTNAME") }}</th>
          <th>{{ t("PERSONNES.COLUMN_LASTNAME") }}</th>
          <th>{{ t("PERSONNES.COLUMN_LOGIN") }}</th>
          <th></th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {% for personne in modele.personnes %}
        <tr>
          <td>{{ personne.titre }}</td>
          <td>{{ personne.prenom }}</td>

          <td><code>{{ personne.login }}</code></td>
          <td class="text-end">
            <div class="d-inline-flex gap-2">
              <a class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary" href="{{ personne.url_modifier }}">{{ t("PERSONNES.EDIT") }}</a>
              {# data-confirmation: a confirmation window will open
                 avant l'envoi du formulaire (cf. static/js/app.js) #}
              <form method="post" action="{{ personne.url_supprimer }}" class="m-0"
                    data-confirmation="{{ t(modele.cles.confirmer_suppression) }}">
                <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">

    </table>
    {% else %}
    <p class="text-muted mb-0">{{ t(modele.cles.vide) }}</p>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
{% endblock %}

A single view for both lists, doctors and clients: the labels specific to each appear in [modele.cles]; [t(modele.cles.titre)] renders a key that is itself a variable. Each row has an “Edit” link and a “Delete” form, which requires confirmation.

docs.title: 11.17.2.4. templates/people/formulaire.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/personnes/formulaire.html - création OU modification d'un
   médecin ou d'un client (ADMIN). modele.creation distingue les deux cas.

   Quand la saisie est refusée (champ vide, login déjà pris...), l'action
   renvoie CETTE vue avec :
     - les valeurs déjà saisies (modele.valeurs) ;
     - les champs fautifs encadrés en rouge (classe Bootstrap "is-invalid") ;
     - sous un champ refusé par la validation, son message ;
     - le message d'erreur de la page, affiché EN BAS de la page par le
       gabarit (cf. fragments/erreurs.html).
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends "layout.html" %}

{% block contenu %}
{% set etat = modele.etat %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{{ t(modele.titre_page) }}</h5>

      {# novalidate: let the SERVEUR be validated (it is the authoritative one);
         les contrôles du navigateur (required...) ne sont qu'un confort,
         qu'un utilisateur peut toujours contourner #}
      <form method="post" action="{{ modele.action }}" novalidate>
        <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
        {% if not modele.creation %}
        <input type="hidden" name="version" value="{{ modele.valeurs.version }}">
        {% endif %}

        {# title, first name, last name: fragment common to three forms #}
        {% include "fragments/champs_personne.html" %}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{{ t("PERSONNES.ACCOUNT_SECTION") }}</h6>

        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">{{ t("PERSONNES.LOGIN_LABEL") }}</label>
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" maxlength="30" autocomplete="off"
                 class="form-control {{ etat.classe_invalide('login') }}" value="{{ modele.valeurs.login }}">
          {% if etat.erreur_de("login") %}
          <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(etat.erreur_de("login")) }}</div>
          {% else %}
          <div class="form-text">{{ t("PERSONNES.LOGIN_HELP_CREATE" if modele.creation else "PERSONNES.LOGIN_HELP_EDIT") }}</div>
          {% endif %}
        </div>

        <div class="mb-4">
          <label class="form-label" for="password">{{ t("PERSONNES.PASSWORD_LABEL") }}</label>
          {# never pre-filled: the password is never sent back to the browser #}
          <input id="password" name="password" type="password" maxlength="72" autocomplete="new-password"
                 class="form-control {{ etat.classe_invalide('password') }}">
          {% if etat.erreur_de("password") %}
          <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(etat.erreur_de("password")) }}</div>
          {% else %}
          <div class="form-text">{{ t("PERSONNES.PASSWORD_HELP_CREATE" if modele.creation else "PERSONNES.PASSWORD_HELP_EDIT") }}</div>
          {% endif %}
        </div>

        <div class="d-flex gap-2">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{{ t("PERSONNES.SAVE") }}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{{ modele.url_liste }}">{{ t("PERSONNES.BACK") }}</a>
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}
  • line 25: the mailing address is provided by the action: [/medecins/ajouter], [/clients/3/modifier]...;
  • lines 27–29: on update, the record version is stored in a hidden field (optimistic lock);
  • line 32: the identity fields;
  • lines 38–44: the login, optional, with a tooltip that depends on whether the record is being created or edited ([t("..." if modele.creation else "...")]);
  • lines 50-50: the password is never pre-filled; it is never sent back to the browser. [autocomplete="new-password"] prevents the browser from suggesting the administrator’s password here.

docs.title: 11.17.2.5. templates/inscription.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/inscription.html - "Créer un compte client" (page publique,
   cf. controllers/inscription.py). Mêmes champs d'identité que le formulaire
   de l'ADMIN (fragment champs_personne.html), mais le login et le mot de
   passe sont obligatoires, avec confirmation.
   Pas de captcha ICI : on n'arrive sur cette page qu'après avoir recopié
   celui de la page d'authentification (bouton "Créer un compte client").

   t(cle, min=...) : le message dont la clé est la valeur de [cle], avec le
   paramètre {min} (cf. web/traducteur.py).
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends "layout.html" %}

{% block contenu %}
{% set etat = modele.etat %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-1">{{ t("INSCRIPTION.TITLE") }}</h5>
      <p class="text-muted small mb-3">{{ t("INSCRIPTION.INTRO") }}</p>

      <form method="post" action="/inscription" novalidate>
        <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
        {% include "fragments/champs_personne.html" %}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{{ t("PERSONNES.ACCOUNT_SECTION") }}</h6>

        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">{{ t("PERSONNES.LOGIN_LABEL") }}</label>
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" maxlength="30" autocomplete="username" required
                 class="form-control {{ etat.classe_invalide('login') }}" value="{{ modele.valeurs.login }}">
          {% if etat.erreur_de("login") %}
          <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(etat.erreur_de("login")) }}</div>
          {% else %}
          <div class="form-text">{{ t("INSCRIPTION.LOGIN_HELP") }}</div>
          {% endif %}
        </div>

        <div class="row g-3 mb-3">
          <div class="col-sm-6">
            <label class="form-label" for="password">{{ t("PERSONNES.PASSWORD_LABEL") }}</label>
            <input id="password" name="password" type="password" maxlength="72" autocomplete="new-password" required
                   class="form-control {{ etat.classe_invalide('password') }}">
            {% if etat.erreur_de("password") %}
            <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(etat.erreur_de("password"), min=modele.mot_de_passe_min) }}</div>
            {% else %}
            <div class="form-text">{{ t("INSCRIPTION.PASSWORD_HELP", min=modele.mot_de_passe_min) }}</div>
            {% endif %}
          </div>
          <div class="col-sm-6">
            <label class="form-label" for="confirmation">{{ t("COMPTE.CONFIRMATION_LABEL") }}</label>
            <input id="confirmation" name="confirmation" type="password" maxlength="72" autocomplete="new-password" required
                   class="form-control {{ etat.classe_invalide('confirmation') }}">
            {% if etat.erreur_de("confirmation") %}
            <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(etat.erreur_de("confirmation")) }}</div>
            {% endif %}
          </div>
        </div>

        <div class="d-flex gap-2">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{{ t("INSCRIPTION.SUBMIT") }}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="/login">{{ t("INSCRIPTION.BACK_TO_LOGIN") }}</a>
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

The customer account creation form: the personal information fields, followed by the username, password, and password confirmation, are required. The message indicating that a password is too short has a parameter specifying the minimum length: [t(etat.erreur_de("password"), min=modele.mot_de_passe_min)]. There is no CAPTCHA here: you can only access this page after entering the CAPTCHA from the login page.

docs.title: 11.17.2.6. templates/espace.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/espace.html - "Mon espace" : la page d'accueil du patient
   (rôle USER), affichée juste après sa connexion.
     - deux options : [Gérer mon compte] et [Voir un agenda] ;
     - son rendez-vous à venir, s'il en a un, avec le moyen de l'annuler.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends "layout.html" %}

{% block contenu %}
  <h4 class="mb-3">{{ t("ESPACE.HELLO", nom=modele.patient) }}</h4>

  <div class="row g-3 mb-4">
    <div class="col-sm-6">
      <a class="card p-4 h-100 text-decoration-none carte-option" href="/mon-compte">
        <h5 class="mb-1">{{ t("ESPACE.MANAGE_ACCOUNT") }}</h5>
        <span class="text-muted">{{ t("ESPACE.MANAGE_ACCOUNT_HELP") }}</span>
      </a>
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6">
      <a class="card p-4 h-100 text-decoration-none carte-option" href="/agenda">
        <h5 class="mb-1">{{ t("ESPACE.VIEW_AGENDA") }}</h5>
        <span class="text-muted">{{ t("ESPACE.VIEW_AGENDA_HELP") }}</span>
      </a>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="card p-3">
    <h5>{{ t("ESPACE.MY_APPOINTMENT") }}</h5>
    {# normally only one (rule: “one upcoming appointment at a time”),
       mais la page sait en afficher plusieurs. loop.last : dernier élément ?
       Le bloc else d'une boucle for : la liste est vide #}
    {% for rv in modele.rendez_vous %}
    <div class="d-flex flex-wrap justify-content-between align-items-center gap-2 py-2{{ '' if loop.last else ' border-bottom' }}">
      <div>
        <div class="fw-semibold">{{ rv.jour }}, {{ rv.horaire }}</div>
        <div class="text-muted">
          <span>{{ rv.medecin }}</span> -
          <a href="{{ rv.url_agenda }}">{{ t("ESPACE.SEE_IN_AGENDA") }}</a>
        </div>
      </div>
      <form method="post" action="/mon-espace/annuler" class="m-0"
            data-confirmation="{{ t('AGENDA.CANCEL_CONFIRM') }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="idRv" value="{{ rv.id }}">
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-outline-danger">{{ t("ESPACE.CANCEL_APPOINTMENT") }}</button>
      </form>
    </div>
    {% else %}
    <p class="text-muted mb-0">{{ t("ESPACE.NO_APPOINTMENT") }}</p>
    {% endfor %}
  </div>
{% endblock %}

The patient’s dashboard: two large tabs (“Manage My Account,” “View Calendar”) and their upcoming appointments. The [for ... else] loop (example 14) displays a message if the list is empty; [loop.last] removes the border below the last appointment. The page can display multiple appointments, even if the management rule allows only one.

docs.title: 11.17.2.7. templates/compte.html
docs.text:
{# =========================================================================
   templates/compte.html - "Gérer mon compte" (rôle USER).
   Deux formulaires indépendants sur la même page :
     1. la modification (identité, login, nouveau mot de passe facultatif) ;
     2. la suppression du compte - qui annule aussi ses rendez-vous.
   L'un comme l'autre exigent le mot de passe ACTUEL.
   ========================================================================= #}
{% extends "layout.html" %}

{% block contenu %}
{% set etat = modele.etat %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">

    {# 1. modification #}
    <div class="card p-4 mb-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{{ t("MON_COMPTE.TITLE") }}</h5>

      <form method="post" action="/mon-compte" novalidate>
        <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="version" value="{{ modele.valeurs.version }}">

        {% include "fragments/champs_personne.html" %}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{{ t("PERSONNES.ACCOUNT_SECTION") }}</h6>

        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">{{ t("PERSONNES.LOGIN_LABEL") }}</label>
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" maxlength="30" autocomplete="username" required
                 class="form-control {{ etat.classe_invalide('login') }}" value="{{ modele.valeurs.login }}">
          {% if etat.erreur_de("login") %}
          <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(etat.erreur_de("login")) }}</div>
          {% endif %}
        </div>

        <div class="row g-3 mb-3">
          <div class="col-sm-6">
            <label class="form-label" for="password">{{ t("MON_COMPTE.NEW_PASSWORD_LABEL") }}</label>
            <input id="password" name="password" type="password" maxlength="72" autocomplete="new-password"
                   class="form-control {{ etat.classe_invalide('password') }}">
            {% if etat.erreur_de("password") %}
            <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(etat.erreur_de("password"), min=modele.mot_de_passe_min) }}</div>
            {% else %}
            <div class="form-text">{{ t("PERSONNES.PASSWORD_HELP_EDIT") }}</div>
            {% endif %}
          </div>
          <div class="col-sm-6">
            <label class="form-label" for="confirmation">{{ t("COMPTE.CONFIRMATION_LABEL") }}</label>
            <input id="confirmation" name="confirmation" type="password" maxlength="72" autocomplete="new-password"
                   class="form-control {{ etat.classe_invalide('confirmation') }}">
            {% if etat.erreur_de("confirmation") %}
            <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(etat.erreur_de("confirmation")) }}</div>
            {% endif %}
          </div>
        </div>

        <div class="mb-4">
          <label class="form-label" for="mot_de_passe_actuel">{{ t("MON_COMPTE.CURRENT_PASSWORD_LABEL") }}</label>
          <input id="mot_de_passe_actuel" name="mot_de_passe_actuel" type="password" maxlength="72"
                 autocomplete="current-password" required
                 class="form-control {{ etat.classe_invalide('mot_de_passe_actuel') }}">
          {% if etat.erreur_de("mot_de_passe_actuel") %}
          <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ t(etat.erreur_de("mot_de_passe_actuel")) }}</div>
          {% else %}
          <div class="form-text">{{ t("MON_COMPTE.CURRENT_PASSWORD_HELP") }}</div>
          {% endif %}
        </div>

        <div class="d-flex gap-2">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{{ t("PERSONNES.SAVE") }}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="/mon-espace">{{ t("MON_COMPTE.BACK") }}</a>
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>

    {# 2. deletion #}
    <div class="card p-4 border-danger">
      <h5 class="card-title text-danger mb-1">{{ t("MON_COMPTE.DELETE_TITLE") }}</h5>
      <p class="text-muted small">{{ t("MON_COMPTE.DELETE_HELP") }}</p>
      <form method="post" action="/mon-compte/supprimer" class="d-flex flex-wrap gap-2 align-items-end"
            data-confirmation="{{ t('MON_COMPTE.DELETE_CONFIRM') }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token() }}">
        <div class="flex-grow-1">
          <label class="form-label" for="mot_de_passe_suppression">{{ t("MON_COMPTE.CURRENT_PASSWORD_LABEL") }}</label>
          <input id="mot_de_passe_suppression" name="mot_de_passe_suppression" type="password" maxlength="72"
                 autocomplete="current-password" required class="form-control">
        </div>
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-danger">{{ t("MON_COMPTE.DELETE_SUBMIT") }}</button>
      </form>
    </div>

  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

Two independent forms on the same page: account modification (lines 19–73) and account deletion (lines 80–89), confirmed by the confirmation window. Both require the current password, entered in two separate fields (a form submits only its own fields).

docs.title: 11.17.2.8. templates/erreur.html

The error area (lines 23–32) is sticky ([position: sticky], [bottom: 1rem]): if the page is taller than the window (a calendar with twelve time slots), it remains visible at the bottom of the window instead of disappearing below the fold. [z-index: 1060] places it above the gray background of modal windows.

docs.title: 11.19.2. static/js/app.js
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// static/js/app.js - the SEUL JavaScript for the application.
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The entire application works without JavaScript. This script adds a
// convenience feature: before submitting a form that includes the
// data-confirmation="...", a modal window asks "Are you sure?"
// (the window itself is located in the page: templates/fragments/confirmation.html).
// If JavaScript is disabled, the form simply submits without
// confirmation—nothing breaks (the principle of “progressive enhancement”).
//
// Why not window.confirm()? Its input field doesn’t format properly, and its
// buttons remain in the browser’s language, not the page’s.
// =========================================================================

(() => {
  const modale = document.getElementById('modale-confirmation');
  if (!modale) {
    return;
  }
  const message = document.getElementById('modale-confirmation-message');
  const boutonNon = modale.querySelector('.modal-footer [data-action="non"]');

  let formulaireEnAttente = null; // the form to submit if you confirm
  let focusPrecedent = null; // the element to focus on when closing

  function ouvrir(formulaire) {
    formulaireEnAttente = formulaire;
    focusPrecedent = document.activeElement;
     // textContent (not innerHTML): the message is displayed as TEXTE,
     // never interpreted as HTML
    message.textContent = formulaire.dataset.confirmation;
    modale.classList.remove('d-none');
     // the focus moves to "No": accidentally pressing Enter does not delete anything
    boutonNon.focus();
  }

  function fermer() {
    modale.classList.add('d-none');
    formulaireEnAttente = null;
    if (focusPrecedent) {
      focusPrecedent.focus();
    }
  }

   // 1. We intercept the submission of forms awaiting confirmation
  document.querySelectorAll('form[data-confirmation]').forEach((formulaire) => {
    formulaire.addEventListener('submit', (evenement) => {
      evenement.preventDefault();
      ouvrir(formulaire);
    });
  });

   // 2. The window’s buttons (Yes / No / close button)
  modale.addEventListener('click', (evenement) => {
    const action = evenement.target.closest('[data-action]')?.dataset.action;
    if (action === 'oui') {
      const formulaire = formulaireEnAttente;
      fermer();
       // formulaire.submit() submits the form; SANS triggers it again
       // the 'submit' event: no new confirmation request
      formulaire.submit();
    } else if (action === 'non') {
      fermer();
    } else if (evenement.target.classList.contains('modal')) {
      fermer(); // Click on the grayed-out background, outside the window
    }
  });

   // 3. Keyboard: Esc closes the window; Tab keeps the focus on the window
   /   / (otherwise, the focus would move to the grayed-out page behind it)
  modale.addEventListener('keydown', (evenement) => {
    if (evenement.key === 'Escape') {
      fermer();
    } else if (evenement.key === 'Tab') {
      const boutons = [...modale.querySelectorAll('button')];
      const premier = boutons[0];
      const dernier = boutons[boutons.length - 1];
      if (evenement.shiftKey && document.activeElement === premier) {
        evenement.preventDefault();
        dernier.focus();
      } else if (!evenement.shiftKey && document.activeElement === dernier) {
        evenement.preventDefault();
        premier.focus();
      }
    }
  });
})();

The script from Example 21, completed:

  • lines 16–18: the script does nothing if the page does not have a confirmation window;
  • lines 26–34: upon opening, the message is placed using [textContent], not [innerHTML]: it is displayed as text and is never interpreted as HTML. The focus moves to the “No” button: accidentally pressing Enter does not delete anything;
  • lines 37–41: Upon closing, the focus returns to the element that had it previously (the “Delete” button), which is important for keyboard navigation;
  • lines 54–65: clicks within the window. [closest('[data-action]')] searches for the element with the attribute [data-action], starting from the clicked element and moving up through its parent elements: a click on an icon inside a button is thus attributed to the button. The operator [?.] returns [undefined] instead of raising an error if no element is found. A click on the grayed-out background closes the window;
  • lines 71–83: keyboard behavior: Esc closes the window; Tab and Shift-Tab cycle the focus among the buttons in the window, without moving to the grayed-out page behind it.

docs.title: 12. Conclusion
docs.text:
This document has presented the development of a MVC web application using the [Flask] framework: an application whose HTML pages are generated by the server, using [Jinja2] views, without a browser-side [JavaScript] framework. He followed the [Spring MVC] course step by step, which itself builds on the [ASP.NET Core MVC] and [NestJS] courses: actions and routing to views, forms, internationalization, security, and data access, followed by a comprehensive case study.

The same 28 examples and the same application were thus written using four frameworks: [TypeScript], [C#], [Java], and [Python]. The concepts are the same; only the names and mechanisms differ. The correspondences between [Spring MVC] and [Flask]:

Spring MVCFlaskclass [@SpringBootApplication], classes [@Configuration], methods [@Bean]factory [create_app], objects stored in [app.extensions]file [pom.xml], starters [Maven]file [requirements.txt], virtual environment, [pip][application.properties], profiles, [@ConfigurationProperties][config.py], [config_<profil>.py], variables [FLASK_...] ([app.config])Dependency injection: singleton beans, [@Service], [@Component]objects created manually by the factory, retrieved by [current_app][@Controller], [@GetMapping], [@PostMapping], view name, or [redirect:...]blueprints, [@bp.get], [@bp.post], [render_template], [redirect]model link, [@RequestParam], converters[request.args], [request.form], [Werkzeug] converters ([<int:id>])[Bean Validation]: [@NotBlank], [@Min], [@Max]..., [@Valid], [BindingResult][Pydantic] (parameters, JSON); [WTForms]: validators, [form.validate()], [form.errors]views [Thymeleaf] ([.html]), [th:text], [th:each], [th:if]views [Jinja2], [{{ }}], [{% for %}], [{% if %}]template and fragments ([th:replace], [th:fragment])[{% extends %}] and blocks, [{% include %}], macros[@ControllerAdvice] and [@ModelAttribute]context processor ([@app.context_processor])flash attributes ([RedirectAttributes])flash messages ([flash], [get_flashed_messages]), in the session cookieservlet filters, interceptorsWSGI, [before_request], [after_request], [teardown_request] middleware[@ControllerAdvice] / [@ExceptionHandler], [ErrorController][@app.errorhandler][Spring Security]: [SecurityFilterChain], resource server, [@PreAuthorize][before_request] and hand-written decorators ([PyJWT], [bcrypt])protection CSRF of [Spring Security][CSRFProtect] from [Flask-WTF]JSON dictionaries read by a [MessageSource], [#{...}], or [LocaleResolver]JSON dictionaries, [t(...)] view function, [g.langue] set by a [before_request][Spring Data JPA] and [Hibernate], [JpaRepository], derived queries, [JPQL][SQLAlchemy]: reporting entities, [select(...)], sessions, handwritten DAO classes[@Transactional], [TransactionTemplate][with sessions.begin() as session:][@Version], managed by [Hibernate][version_id_col], managed by [SQLAlchemy][mvnw spring-boot:run], [Spring Boot DevTools][python app.py] in debug mode (automatic reload)executable archive ([java -jar]), with [Tomcat] includedWSGI server: [Waitress], [Gunicorn]

Compared to [Spring MVC], the key points to note are:

  • [Flask] is a micro-framework: it provides routing, requests and responses, the [Jinja2] views, and session management—and that’s it. Everything else (validation, forms, security, data access, translation) is handled by libraries chosen by the developer or written by the developer. This means more code to write, but the code is transparent: nothing happens “by magic,” and you can track every object from its creation (in [create_app]) to its use;
  • there is no dependency injection container: shared objects are created by the factory, stored in [app.extensions], and retrieved by [current_app]. For an application of this size, it’s simple and sufficient;
  • The objects [request], [g], [session], and [current_app] are proxies that, during a request, refer to the objects of that request. They eliminate the need to pass the query from one function to another, but can only be used while processing a query (or within a manually created application context);
  • the decorators of [Python] serve the same purpose as the annotations of [Java]: routes, tags ([@publique]), and access controls ([@roles_requis]). But a decorator is simply a function that you can write yourself in just a few lines;
  • [Python] is a dynamically typed language: type annotations ([list[Medecin]], [Protocol], generic classes) document the code and guide the editor, but are not checked at runtime. Tools such as [Pylance] (in [Visual Studio Code]) or [mypy] check them before execution;
  • [SQLAlchemy] requires writing the DAO layer (a few lines per request), but its requests—constructed using [Python] objects—remain close to the SQL they produce, and displaying the SQL ([SQL_ECHO]) commands allows you to verify what is being sent to the database. Loading relations is explicitly controlled, query by query;
  • The [Jinja2] views mix HTML and [{{ }}] / [{% %}] tags: they are not valid HTML pages like those of [Thymeleaf], but their language, similar to [Python], is powerful (filters, macros, template inheritance), and automatic escaping protects against HTML injection.

The case study shows that a classic HTML application, without the essential [JavaScript], remains a simple and robust solution: each page is a URL, the browser’s “Back” button works, and the server controls everything. The limited use of [JavaScript] (confirmation windows) enhances the user experience without being necessary for the application to function.

For more information, you can consult the documentation for [Flask] (flask.palletsprojects.com), [Jinja2] (jinja.palletsprojects.com), [Werkzeug] (werkzeug.palletsprojects.com), [WTForms] (wtforms.readthedocs.io), and [Flask-WTF] (flask-wtf.readthedocs.io), from [SQLAlchemy] (docs.sqlalchemy.org), from [Pydantic] (docs.pydantic.dev), and compare this application with its counterparts [Spring MVC], [ASP.NET Core MVC], and [NestJS].

docs.title: 6. Data Scopes
docs.text:
A web application serves many users at once, and each user makes numerous requests. Data can therefore be shared at several levels, known as its scope:

  • application scope: the data is shared by all users for the entire lifetime of the server (the list of doctors, for example);
  • request scope: the data exists only for the duration of a single request (a view’s model, the logged-in user as identified for that request);
  • client scope: the data is specific to a user and must persist from one request to the next (the selected language, the logged-in user).

Web applications have long used a server-maintained session for this last scope: a memory specific to each browser, identified via an identification cookie ([JSESSIONID] in [Java], [PHPSESSID] to [PHP]). The session for [Flask] is different: as we saw in Example 20, it is stored in a signed cookie on the client’s side. The server does not store anything between two requests from the same user: it is said to be stateless. This is what makes it possible, for example, to run multiple identical servers behind a load balancer: any one of them can handle any request. The trade-off is that a cookie is under the user’s control; the user can read it and attempt to modify it. Therefore, only non-sensitive data is stored there, and—if the data must be trusted—it is signed by the server, which then detects any modifications: this is the case for the session [Flask] and the authentication token (see the chapter on authentication).

In [Flask], each scope has its own container:

ScopeSupportLifetimeapplicationAn object created at startup, stored in [app.extensions] and retrieved by [current_app] (example 06)The entire server lifetime, shared by all requestsRequestThe object [g], and the object [request] itself (example 16)processing a requestsessionthe object [session], a dictionary stored in a signed cookieuntil the browser is closed (by default)clienta standard cookie set by [set_cookie] (example 22)the duration set by [max_age]

The objects [current_app], [g], [request], and [session] are imported from the package [flask]. These are proxies (example 05): during a request, each one identifies the object of that request (or of the application processing it).

docs.title: 6.1.1. The objects: services/compteur.py
docs.text:
# services/compteur.py: a shared counter and request information
from itertools import count
from threading import Lock


# scope APPLICATION: a single instance (see app.py)
class CompteurService:

    def __init__(self):
        self._total = 0
         # multiple requests can run EN MÊME TEMPS: the lock ensures
         # that two simultaneous increments are not lost
        self._verrou = Lock()

    def incrementer(self) -> int:
        with self._verrou:
            self._total += 1
            return self._total


# scope REQUÊTE: one instance per query (see app.py, "debut" function)
class RequeteInfos:

     # a counter shared by all instances (attribute of CLASSE);
     # next(...) is atomic: two threads never obtain the same number
    _instances = count(1)

    def __init__(self, debut: str):
        self.numero = next(RequeteInfos._instances)
        self.debut = debut
  • Lines 7–18: a visit counter, with application scope: a single object, shared by all requests. As with the task list in Example 20, a lock protects the increment: the [self._total += 1] statement is not atomic (it reads the value, increments it, then writes it), and two threads executing it simultaneously could read the same value—resulting in a visit being lost;
  • lines 22–30: query-scope information: one object per query, containing a number and the time of the query. The number is derived from a counter shared by all instances: [count(1)], from the standard module [itertools], is an iterator that produces 1, 2, 3... each time [next] is called. This is a class attribute (declared at the class level, not in the constructor): it is shared by all instances.

# app.py: the application from Example 23
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

from flask import Blueprint, Flask, g

from controllers.portees import portees
from services.compteur import CompteurService, RequeteInfos

BOOTSTRAP = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "commun" / "bootstrap"


def create_app():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    app.jinja_env.trim_blocks = True
    app.jinja_env.lstrip_blocks = True
     # the key that signs the session cookie (scope SESSION)
    app.config["SECRET_KEY"] = "une-cle-secrete-pour-l-exemple-23"
     # scope APPLICATION: a single object, created at startup, shared by TOUTES
     # requests from TOUS users
    app.extensions["compteur"] = CompteurService()
    app.register_blueprint(Blueprint("bootstrap", __name__, static_folder=BOOTSTRAP,
                                     static_url_path="/bootstrap"))
    app.register_blueprint(portees)

     # scope REQUÊTE: the object g is created and destroyed with each request. This
     # function, executed by the AVANT action, stores an object representing both the action and the
     # view will access during the CETTE request
    @app.before_request
    def debut():
        g.infos = RequeteInfos(datetime.now().strftime("%H:%M:%S.%f")[:-3])

    return app


if __name__ == "__main__":
    create_app().run(port=5000, debug=True)
  • line 18: the key that signs the session cookie;
  • line 21: the application-scope object;
  • lines 29–31: Before each request, a [RequeteInfos] object is stored in [g]. The action and the view will retrieve it, but only during this request. [strftime("%H:%M:%S.%f")] formats the time with its microseconds ([%f], six digits); [[:-3]] removes the last three characters from the string, leaving the milliseconds.

docs.text:
# controllers/portees.py: the four data scopes
from flask import Blueprint, current_app, g, make_response, render_template, request, session

portees = Blueprint("portees", __name__)


@portees.get("/")
def afficher():
     # APPLICATION: the shared counter
    total = current_app.extensions["compteur"].incrementer()
     # SESSION: a dictionary specific to the CE browser, which Flask stores in a
     # SIGNÉ (session) cookie; it lasts until the browser is closed
    session["visites"] = session.get("visites", 0) + 1
     # CLIENT: data stored by NAVIGATEUR in a regular cookie,
     # sent back to the server with every request
    mes_visites = vers_entier(request.cookies.get("mesVisites")) + 1
    reponse = make_response(render_template(
        "portees/portees.html", total=total, instance=g.infos.numero,
        visites_session=session["visites"], mes_visites=mes_visites))
    reponse.set_cookie("mesVisites", str(mes_visites), httponly=True, samesite="Lax")
    return reponse


# "41" -> 41; None or "abc" -> 0
def vers_entier(texte: str | None) -> int:
    try:
        return int(texte)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return 0
  • line 10: the application scope. [current_app] refers to the application processing the current request;
  • line 13: the session scope. [session] is used as a dictionary: [session.get("visites", 0)] returns the value of the key, or 0 if it is absent. When the action modifies the session, [Flask] sends, along with the response, a new cookie, [session], which contains the signed dictionary;
  • line 16: the client scope, with a regular cookie, [mesVisites], read from [request.cookies]. Its value is a string provided by the browser and may therefore be missing or invalid; the function [vers_entier] returns 0 in either case;
  • Lines 17–20: To set a cookie, you need the response object: [make_response] constructs it from the page generated by the view (example 05), then [set_cookie] adds the header [Set-Cookie] to it. Without [max_age], the cookie lasts until the browser is closed (it is a “session” cookie, as defined by browsers);
  • line 18: the request scope: the object stored in [g] by the function [debut].

docs.title: 6.1.5. Execution
docs.text:
After two visits in a browser:

Let's track the requests using [curl], which acts as an initial browser by storing its cookies in the file [a.txt]:

curl -i -c a.txt -b a.txt http://localhost:5000/

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 595
Set-Cookie: mesVisites=1; HttpOnly; Path=/; SameSite=Lax
Set-Cookie: session=eyJ2aXNpdGVzIjoxfQ.arfKwA.Q05nRwG-I_EsAKciaI87smp-DDY; HttpOnly; Path=/
...
      <li>application : 1 visite(s) du site, tous navigateurs confondus</li>
      <li>requête : objet n° 2 (n° 2 dans la vue),
        requête reçue à 15:38:08.535</li>
      <li>session : 1 visite(s) de ce navigateur (1 dans la vue)</li>
      <li>client : 1 visite(s) de ce navigateur</li>
...

The response sets two cookies. The first, [mesVisites], contains the value in plain text. The second, [session], contains the session dictionary: the portion before the first period is JSON [{"visites":1}], encoded in Base64 (uncompressed this time, since it is short); followed by the date and the signature.

The request scope object has the number 2, even though this is the first visit to the page: this is because the [debut] function runs before every request received by the application, including requests for which no action exists (in this case, a request for a nonexistent URL, made just before) and requests for static files. In the browser, each page thus triggers a second request for the stylesheet of [Bootstrap]: hence the odd numbers in the screenshot. A second visit, with the same cookies:

curl -i -c a.txt -b a.txt http://localhost:5000/

Set-Cookie: mesVisites=2; HttpOnly; Path=/; SameSite=Lax
Set-Cookie: session=eyJ2aXNpdGVzIjoyfQ.arfKwA.D9rLAmX6E4r5SiWa6DaPmLr_Cl0; HttpOnly; Path=/
...
      <li>application : 2 visite(s) du site, tous navigateurs confondus</li>
      <li>requête : objet n° 3 (n° 3 dans la vue),
        requête reçue à 15:38:08.552</li>
      <li>session : 2 visite(s) de ce navigateur (2 dans la vue)</li>
      <li>client : 2 visite(s) de ce navigateur</li>

A second “browser,” with its own cookie file, initially empty:

curl -c b.txt -b b.txt http://localhost:5000/

      <li>application : 3 visite(s) du site, tous navigateurs confondus</li>
      <li>requête : objet n° 4 (n° 4 dans la vue),
        requête reçue à 15:38:08.565</li>
      <li>session : 1 visite(s) de ce navigateur (1 dans la vue)</li>
      <li>client : 1 visite(s) de ce navigateur</li>

The application counter has continued running; the session and cookie for the second browser start over at 1. Finally, a malicious user forges their own cookies: 1,000 visits in [mesVisites], and a session that purports to contain [{"visites":999}] (Base64-encoded as [eyJ2aXNpdGVzIjo5OTl9]), with the signature of another session:

curl -b "mesVisites=1000;session=eyJ2aXNpdGVzIjo5OTl9.arfKuA.chOe9TXdLhGaUJOQo0QMT_hbPnE" http://localhost:5000/

      <li>application : 4 visite(s) du site, tous navigateurs confondus</li>
      ...
      <li>session : 1 visite(s) de ce navigateur (1 dans la vue)</li>
      <li>client : 1001 visite(s) de ce navigateur</li>

The regular cookie was accepted as is: 1,001 visits. The forged session, however, was rejected: its signature does not match its content, and [Flask] ignored it, as if it were absent. That is the key difference between a regular cookie and a signed cookie. Let’s remember the rule: data coming from the client is only trustworthy if it is signed by the server; and even when signed, it remains readable: we don’t put anything secret in it.

The case study brings them together into a complete, realistic-sized application (80 files, approximately 5,300 lines, including comments). It was written with the same care as the examples: each file begins with a comment explaining its role, and tricky sections are annotated in the code. Each main folder also contains a file named [README.md] that lists its files. The document’s comments highlight what the examples did not show and refer to the examples for the rest.

docs.title: 5. Internationalization
docs.text:
An internationalized application displays its text in the user's language. The case study is in French and English. The principle is simple: the views no longer contain text, but rather keys ([MENU.ACCUEIL]), and a dictionary for each language associates a text with each key. The selected language is stored in a cookie.

The [Flask] ecosystem offers an extension for this purpose, [Flask-Babel], which relies on the standard translation system [gettext]: texts are extracted from the code by a tool, translated into [.po] files, and then compiled into [.mo] files. It is a powerful system, but it requires specific tools and a compilation step. Instead, we’ll write a small class that reads JSON dictionaries: These are the same files as the [ASP.NET Core MVC], [NestJS], and [Spring MVC] versions from the case study, and their format can be read and written without any special tools. The [Babel] library, on the other hand, is still used for formatting dates and amounts (Example 16).

docs.title: 5.1.1. Dictionaries
docs.text:
The [i18n/fr.json] file:

{
  "MENU": {
    "ACCUEIL": "Accueil",
    "PRODUITS": "Produits"
  },
  "ACCUEIL": {
    "TITRE": "Bienvenue",
    "BONJOUR": "Bonjour {nom} !",
    "DATE": "Nous sommes le {date}."
  },
  "PRODUITS": {
    "TITRE": "Nos produits",
    "NOM": "Produit",
    "PRIX": "Prix",
    "NOMBRE": "{n} produit(s) au catalogue."
  }
}

The keys are grouped by theme within nested JSON objects: the menu text “Home” has the full key [MENU.ACCUEIL]. A text string may contain placeholders, written as [{nom}], which are replaced during translation. The file [i18n/en.json] has exactly the same keys:

    "ACCUEIL": "Home",
    "PRODUITS": "Products"
  },
  "ACCUEIL": {
    "TITRE": "Welcome",
    "BONJOUR": "Hello {nom}!",
    "DATE": "Today is {date}."
  },
  "PRODUITS": {
    "TITRE": "Our products",
    "NOM": "Product",
    "PRIX": "Price",
    "NOMBRE": "{n} product(s) in the catalogue."
  }
}

docs.title: 5.1.2. The translation service: translation/traducteur.py
docs.text:
# translation/traducteur.py: the translation service
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

from flask import g


class Traducteur:

    LANGUES = ("fr", "en")
    LANGUE_PAR_DEFAUT = "fr"

     # {name}: a parameter in a text
    PARAMETRE = re.compile(r"\{(\w+)\}")

    def __init__(self, dossier: Path):
         # language -> (full key "ACCUEIL.BONJOUR" -> text)
        self._dictionnaires: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
        for langue in self.LANGUES:
            with open(dossier / f"{langue}.json", encoding="utf-8") as fichier:
                self._dictionnaires[langue] = self._aplatir(json.load(fichier))

     # the supported language corresponding to [code]: "en" -> "en"; "de" or None -> "fr"
    @classmethod
    def langue(cls, code: str | None) -> str:
        return code if code in cls.LANGUES else cls.LANGUE_PAR_DEFAUT

     # translate("ACCUEIL.BONJOUR", name="Marie") -> "Hello Marie!", in the
     # language of the current request (g.langue, see app.py)
    def traduire(self, cle: str, **parametres) -> str:
         # If a key is missing, the key itself is displayed: an omission is visible on the screen
        texte = self._dictionnaires[g.langue].get(cle, cle)
         # Each {name} is replaced by the value of the parameter with the same name
        return self.PARAMETRE.sub(
            lambda m: str(parametres.get(m.group(1), m.group(0))), texte)

     # { "MENU": { "ACCUEIL": "Home" } } -> { "MENU.ACCUEIL": "Home" }
    @classmethod
    def _aplatir(cls, noeud: dict, prefixe: str = "") -> dict[str, str]:
        resultat = {}
        for cle, valeur in noeud.items():
            cle_complete = f"{prefixe}.{cle}" if prefixe else cle
            if isinstance(valeur, dict):
                resultat.update(cls._aplatir(valeur, cle_complete))
            else:
                resultat[cle_complete] = valeur
        return resultat
  • lines 11–12: supported languages and the default language—class attributes shared by all objects of the class and accessible without an object ([Traducteur.LANGUES]);
  • line 15: the regular expression for a parameter: a curly brace ([\{], preceded by a [\] because the curly brace has a specific meaning in regular expressions), one or more word characters ([\w+]), and a closing curly brace. The parentheses capture the parameter name. [re.compile] parses the expression once and for all;
  • lines 17–22: the constructor reads the dictionaries once, when the service is created. [json.load] converts the contents of a JSON file into [Python] objects (nested dictionaries). [with open(...) as fichier] opens the file and ensures it is closed at the end of the block; [encoding="utf-8"] is essential, because the default encoding depends on the system (under [Windows], it is not always [UTF-8]);
  • Lines 25–27: A class method ([@classmethod] decorator) takes the class ([cls]) instead of an object; it is called on the class: [Traducteur.langue("en")]. It returns the supported language corresponding to a code, or the default language if the code is unknown or missing;
  • lines 31–36: the translation of a key, in the language of the current query, read from [g.langue] (see Example 16). A key missing from the dictionary is displayed as-is: an omission is immediately visible on the screen. The parameters are received as named parameters ([**parametres]); the regular expression method [sub] replaces each parameter found in the text with the result of a function—in this case, an anonymous function ([lambda m: ...])—which receives the match found ([m]): [m.group(1)] is the captured name, [m.group(0)] is the full text [{nom}], which is retained if the parameter was not provided;
  • Lines 40–48: The nested JSON objects are “flattened” into a single dictionary, whose keys are the full keys: [{"MENU": {"ACCUEIL": "Accueil"}}] becomes [{"MENU.ACCUEIL": "Accueil"}]. The method is recursive: it calls itself for each nested object, using the current key as a prefix.
